EXCLUSIVE: Steven Spielberg’s L.A. Ranch Sells for $8 Million Below Asking—Just 2 Months After Hitting the Market

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (916 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Filmmaker Steven Spielberg has sold the sprawling Los Angeles ranch where he housed his horses for $22.3 million—just two months after listing the palatial estate.
  • Spielberg, 79, and his wife, Kate Capshaw, 72, purchased the property in 1999 through their corporate entity, Texas Tart, for $5.75 million.
  • Industry observers note that they listed the massive compound in September for $30 million.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Filmmaker Steven Spielberg has sold the sprawling Los Angeles ranch where he housed his horses for $22.3 million—just two months after listing the palatial estate.

Spielberg, 79, and his wife, Kate Capshaw, 72, purchased the property in 1999 through their corporate entity, Texas Tart, for $5.75 million.

Industry observers note that they listed the massive compound in September for $30 million. Then, in late October, the home disappeared from the market with no indication why.

Now, Realtor.com® can exclusively reveal that the property has traded hands, selling for $22.3 million—at a nearly $8 million discount.

When they purchased the home, the Hollywood mogul and actress unveiled ambitious plans to dramatically overhaul the estate with a 27,000-square-foot, five-story riding facility featuring a domed roof and underground horse stables.

Spielberg's vision reportedly included more than $7 million in renovations, as well as aims to construct a 2,400-square-foot guesthouse and a three-story guardhouse.

However, neighbors objected to the scale of the project. While the Oscar-winning director reportedly planned to present revised ideas to his neighbors, the elaborate project ultimately never came to fruition. Meanwhile, he did update the estate into the magnificent abode it is today.

It has been revealed that the property was held by Spielberg and Capshaw for nearly three decades. Last month, the couple decided to finally part ways with the equestrian retreat, listing it for $29.9 million with Sandro Dazzan of The Agency.

Known as Dogwood, the seven-bedroom, 9.5-bathroom estate sits on 2.8 acres in the secluded Sullivan Canyon. It offers an impressive array of equestrian amenities alongside its luxurious living spaces.

"Nestled in the ultra-private Sullivan Canyon, Dogwood is Los Angeles' premiere equestrian ranch—a rare masterpiece designed by renowned architect Michael Kovac with interiors by Michael Smith and landscape design by Christine London," the listing stated.

Spanning two parcels, the property combines a sophisticated country-inspired aesthetic with extensive facilities designed for horses, entertaining, and guests.

Inside the main residence, rich walnut floors and wood-covered ceilings create a warm atmosphere, while expansive windows bring in plenty of natural light.

The spacious living room offers multiple seating areas anchored by dual fireplaces, creating an inviting space for relaxing and entertaining.

That rustic aesthetic continues into the chef's kitchen, which features extensive wood cabinetry, an oversized center island, high-end appliances, and an eat-in dining nook.

"The chef's kitchen with eat-in dining nook and wood-burning fireplace connects to a cozy family room and IPE-clad terrace overlooking a tranquil reflection pond," the listing noted.

Upstairs, the primary suite offers a peaceful retreat complete with a wood-burning fireplace and access to a private covered terrace.

The outdoor space boasts yet another fireplace along with sweeping city and canyon views, according to the listing.

Elsewhere inside the home is a media room that can double as a game room, as well as a wine cellar.

But the property's most impressive features are arguably those designed for its four-legged residents.

Across from the main entertaining spaces sits a six-stall barn complete with an executive office, staff quarters, three grooming stations, a feed kitchen, and storage.

The equestrian facility is topped off by a sprawling 20,000-square-foot riding arena with an observation deck and mirrored wall, which the listing notes is suitable for both dressage and jumping.

The estate's lower parcel expands the compound with a stylish one-bedroom guesthouse equipped with its own kitchen, rooftop deck, and basement office and storage spaces.

There is also a second four-stall barn, a 5,400-square-foot turnout area, a private gate, and parking for more than 10 vehicles.

Both parcels are supported by a security command post and generators. The ranch is surrounded by lush landscaping, while a tranquil reflection pond adds to its secluded, countryside atmosphere—despite the estate's location in the heart of Los Angeles.

With this $29.9 million listing, Spielberg and Capshaw are closing a decades-long chapter. Even without having resided in this property, the couple aren't short on lavish abodes to call home.

Their main residence is a stunning Pacific Palisades abode, which has served as their home since 1985.

The property spans 20,000 square feet and boasts a media room, a 14,000-gallon aquarium, and several other lavish amenities.

Over in Malibu, they own a beachfront abode, which is made up of two parcels.

They purchased the first parcel in 1989 for $3.3 million and the second in 2000 for $3.2 million.

The home is situated on a 1.44-acre lot and boasts 144 feet of ocean frontage.

They also hold the keys to a dwelling in Newly introduced York, which they purchased in 1983.

The couple snapped up the 6-acre estate and enlisted architect Charles Gwathmey to overhaul the abode.

Over the years, he added horse stables and a lavish guesthouse.

In 2008, he expanded the property by picking up a 3.2-acre pond in the front of the home for $20 million.

Also on the East Coast, the couple own a 6,000-square-foot apartment building in Manhattan.

Latest Update: Bootstrapped startup Levenza brings consumer-style personal agents to business workers

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1231 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence enthusiasts are embracing personal agents that can automate life’s most tedious digital chores, but office workers are still stuck juggling calendars, email messages and chat threads.
  • In a recent development, levenza wants to change that with the launch of what it notes are the first personal AI agents designed for corporate employees.
  • Industry observers note that in the last few months, personal AI agents have emerged as the hottest new trend in AI, sparking fierce competition among both technology giants and agentic startups.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 08:00 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

Artificial intelligence enthusiasts are embracing personal agents that can automate life’s most tedious digital chores, but office workers are still stuck juggling calendars, email messages and chat threads.

In a recent development, levenza wants to change that with the launch of what it notes are the first personal AI agents designed for corporate employees. The startup today announced the general availability of its enterprise-grade personal agents, together with its first acquisition in the shape of the AI research lab Fluid Inference.

Industry observers note that in the last few months, personal AI agents have emerged as the hottest new trend in AI, sparking fierce competition among both technology giants and agentic startups. The biggest name is probably Meta Platforms Inc.’s Muse, a “secure by design” personal assistant that quickly shot to the top of U.S. app charts following its launch in September. We’ve also seen OpenAI’s Dots, powered by GPT-6 Astra, which aim to proactively get work done on behalf of their people, as well as startups such as Instinct, which raised a colossal $1 billion in funding in September for its consumer-focused agents.

In a recent development, AI agents may still be somewhat divisive, but the early success of Muse, Dots and Instinct shows that there’s clearly a large market for automated assistants. Yet those tools are all targeted primarily at consumers rather than enterprise workers, which means there’s a massive gap in the market that’s waiting to be filled. Levenza wants to be the one that fills it, with its personal agents developed specifically to run inside sensitive corporate environments.

Co-founder and Chief Executive Haefa Mansour (pictured, left) told SiliconANGLE that the difference between Levenza’s agents and those of its competitors is that it takes time to work with individual companies to customize what they can and can’t do. She explained that workplace agents can only provide value if they’re able to connect to corporate systems securely and respect a tech giant’s dynamics and security policies.

According to recent reports, “People have seen what personal AI agents can do outside of work, and they’re expecting the same experience inside the office,” Mansour said. “But most people at work are still spending hours every week coordinating schedules, cha50sing replies and tracking tasks. We built Levenza to take responsibility for that work.”.

Recent findings suggest that levenza’s personal agents are designed to live inside of the platforms where work gets done, such as Microsoft Teams, Outlook and Slack. Within those environments, they act as proactive digital assistants for senior executives and other professionals.

It has been revealed that among other things, they can coordinate meetings across time zones, book hotel rooms, liaise with travel agencies, submit timesheets, triage overflowing email inboxes and send out replies and follow-ups when necessary. The more they do this work, the more they learn about the individual worker they’re serving, allowing them to become more useful over time, Mansour said.

It has been revealed that by automating and coordinating routine work, Levenza’s agents can free workers from the “administrative drag” that affects every worker, slowing down productivity. “Microsoft’s 2025 Work Trend Index found that the average worker receives 117 emails per day and is interrupted every two minutes,” Mansour said. “On top of the inbox and the calendar come the travel, expenses and follow-ups that slip through the cracks – none of this is work that professionals were actually hired to do.”.

It has been revealed that mansour, a former Bain & Co. alumni who holds a Ph.D. from the University of California, founded Levenza alongside former Databricks Inc. and Uber Technologies Inc. engineer Austin Tackaberry (right) specifically to eliminate these distractions. The startup has made impressive traction, and despite not raising a dime in outside funding, its personal agents are already up and running at more than 300 enterprise customers, serving more than 10,000 professionals at those customers.

In a recent development, early adopters such as Hg Capital and Oliver Wyman LLC report that their employees are saving up to three hours daily by offloading mundane admin to Levenza’s personal agents. They can also deal with any problems that occur during someone’s day. “For instance, if a manager’s customer workshop is running late and they’re likely to miss their flight, they don’t need to worry,” Mansour said. “Levenza will reach out to the travel management company to rebook according to their updated schedule.”.

This means the manager in question will be able to focus on the workshop, safe in the knowledge that they’ll still be able to get to where they need to go after it does finish.

Industry observers note that the acquisition of Fluid Inference is all about making Levenza’s agents more accessible. Mansour said the startup is an open-source research lab that’s focused on developing AI speech and ambient intelligence models.

By buying it, Levenza will be able to integrate natural voice interactions with its agents, so workers won’t have to tell them what needs to be done. Fluid Inference’s founder Brandon Weng is going to stick around as Levenza’s upcoming head of engineering, adding much-needed talent to its team.

With Levenza’s agents now generally available, Mansour indicates the manufacturer will use its growing revenues to expand its third-party integrations and develop more capabilities for them. The company aims to launch automations for travel booking and expense management early next year, but that’s just the beginning.

“In the future, Levenza agents will operate with full autonomy in the enterprise, proactively deciding what work needs to be done,” she noted. “They’ll coordinate with groups of other Levenza agents to collectively accomplish tasks.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Secret Lives of Mormon Wives" star Taylor Frankie Paul is turning her attention to real estate, sharing a look at her first investment property after recently becoming a homeowner on her own.

The TV personality has been documenting the next step in her property journey on Instagram, sharing a reel that puts her renovation skills on full display.

Sources indicate that paul, 32, took to social media to reveal that her first townhouse rental property is ready to welcome its first guest, captioning the clip, "My first townhouse rental property is now ready for move in (I’ll link info)Thanks to my family being the dream team. Mother is the agent to contact. Father is the general contractor, my brother and family friend skip all helped put it together. Thank you all so much.".

Sources indicate that paul announced in September that she had closed on her first rental property. She said she was excited to begin something she had wanted to do for a long time, and described her focus as “renovations and rentals.” Her mother, Liann May, helped her with the purchase as her real estate agent, while her father is a general contractor.

The video put the charming dwelling on full display, revealing the property sprawled across multiple levels and boasted several bedrooms and bathrooms.

According to recent reports, the first floor featured wood flooring, while the upstairs came complete with carpet flooring. The chef's kitchen boasted all-white cabinetry and state-of-the-art appliances.

Paul also shared images from the renovation process, revealing that she was heavily involved in painting the property, picking the right tiles, swatching carpet looks, and more.

Sources indicate that paul even posed in the property, highlighting her pride at finishing the project. The reality TV alum has not shared the rental price or listing.

Her venture into real estate comes just months splashed out an impressive $1 million on her new Utah home—snapping up a "spacious" seven-bedroom dwelling in one of Salt Lake City's most sought-after suburbs.

Paul revealed in an emotional Instagram post shared in May that she had closed on her first property as a "solo homeowner," while praising her mother for helping her find the dwelling where she will start her next chapter.

In June, property records revealed that the home in question is a stunning and very "spacious" dwelling located in an upscale Salt Lake City suburb; the property was originally listed for $979,000, however records show that Paul paid above ask, with the final sale price listed in the deed as $1,000,160.

The 4,100-square-foot home, which was built in 2006, offers more than enough space for Paul and her three children—daughter Indy, 8, and son Ocean, 5, whom she shares with ex-husband Tate Paul, and son Ever, 2, whose father is Paul's former partner, Dakota Mortensen.

It boasts seven bedrooms, 3.5 bathrooms, and has a wealth of living space, including a large open-plan kitchen and living area, complete with its own fireplace, as well as a finished basement that features its own separate entrance and was described in the listing as being an ideal spot for guest accommodation or an in-law suite.

Outside, there are plenty of amenities that will no doubt be used by Paul and her kids, including a basketball court, a hot tub, and a covered patio that would be ideal for hosting outdoor dinners.

But while Paul may well be delighted with her latest spread, she has previously admitted that leaving her former Utah property has not been easy.

The TV personality admitted in a candid post shared on her social media accounts that the transition has been emotionally overwhelming because of the attachment she formed to her previous dwelling and the experiences tied to it.

Recent findings suggest that "Call me pessimist Paul at this point, because I in fact feel all the feelings leaving a home too," she wrote. "Once it’s empty I sit in it and reminisce in the memories. I thought Geminis are known to adapt easily??

"Yet I have the hardest time with goodbyes in any way, even if I know how exciting the next part is. Today was such an exciting move and I couldn’t help to bawl my eyes out.".

In the post, Paul shared an image of herself crying, as well as a moving van.

She also shared snaps of her children in her old Utah home.

Paul also hinted at the bittersweet experience when she announced that she had closed on the property, while sharing a video of herself signing the closing documents for her fresh abode, along with pictures that showed her posing with a giant key.

The milestone moment came in the wake of a very turbulent few months for Paul, who split from her former partner, Mortensen, amid a spate of domestic violence allegations levied by both parties—a scandal that saw her season of "The Bachelorette" dropped by ABC, before it was reported that the reality star would not be returning to Hulu's "The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.".

Industry observers note that "Officially a solo home owner and thank you to the best real estate agent in Utah, Liann May," she wrote in the caption. "I see the sadness through the excitement but I am trying.".

It marks the first time that the mother of three has owned her own abode, having previously revealed that she has spent much of her adult life renting.

Paul previously teased her homeowner era during an Instagram Story on May 6, where she revealed, “I just bought my first house on my own. [I had] been renting for years.”.

The home purchase comes after a difficult year for the Hulu personality, whose highly publicized relationship with Mortensen played out both online and on-screen during recent seasons of "The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.".

Paul and Mortensen—who share son Ever together—split after a series of explosive public allegations and legal disputes, including domestic violence accusations that made headlines earlier this year.

The reality star has since been open about wanting a “fresh start,” previously sharing emotional videos of herself packing up her former home while navigating the breakup and co-parenting challenges.

Now, however, Paul appears focused on rebuilding her life independently—with the latest Utah property symbolizing a major turning point, both personally and financially.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The integration is aimed at the routine calls that make up much of a health system’s phone traffic, such as booking a visit, refilling a prescription or asking about a bill.
  • Grok Voice is a speech-to-speech model from SpaceXSI that is said to offer subsecond time to first audio, native tool use and the ability to reason while it speaks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

According to recent reports, healthcare artificial intelligence company Innovaccer Inc. today confirmed that it has expanded its Gravity Voice AI agents with Grok Voice, the speech-to-speech model from Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company SpaceXSI, formerly xAI.

The integration is aimed at the routine calls that make up much of a health system’s phone traffic, such as booking a visit, refilling a prescription or asking about a bill.

Grok Voice is a speech-to-speech model from SpaceXSI that is said to offer subsecond time to first audio, native tool use and the ability to reason while it speaks. According to Innovaccer, the model was trained on real phone audio with interruptions, corrections and background noise in it. More than 25 languages are supported. A business associate agreement is available for Grok Voice, which is Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act-eligible.

Coming into the expansion, Innovaccer’s voice business has grown swiftly. Patient voice interactions on the platform have gone from roughly 250,000 to more than five million in the six months since the agents went live. Customers using them are remarked to be booking significantly more appointments, with referral intakes tripled and documentation time per case down 90%.

“Healthcare Voice AI is moving from answering questions to doing work,” co-founder and Chief Executive Abhinav Shashank noted. With Grok Voice, he said, the company is extending where its agents work across the healthcare journey.

Industry observers note that innovaccer’s Agents of Care on Gravity approach is designed so that software handles the bulk of administrative calls, such as scheduling and refills. A human stays in the loop on clinical conversations.

Existing customers will get Grok Voice first through upgrades, along with newly introduced customer deployments. Innovaccer looks to use it in scheduling, referrals, prior authorizations, refill requests, chronic care check-ins and annual wellness visit outreach, among other tasks.

According to recent reports, the integration is set to extend beyond voice over time. Innovaccer indicates it will bring Grok models to its healthcare data through the Grok API, with plans for SpaceXSI’s Grok Build coding agent and Grok Bot AI agent as well. Healthcare-specific training and evaluation are to follow once the voice integration is live.

Industry observers note that the integration comes about six weeks after SpaceXSI released Grok Voice 3.0, the latest version of the model. At the time, SpaceXSI said Starlink uses Grok Voice to answer about 20,000 customer calls a day, with roughly 70% resolved without a human. The SpaceXSI name was adopted earlier in October, following SpaceX’s acquisition of xAI in February and a rename to SpaceXAI in July.

Innovaccer is a venture capital-backed company that has raised about $675 million to date, including a $275 million Series F round in January 2025. Notable customers include Orlando Health, Adventist HealthCare and Banner Health.

Gravity Voice AI agents with Grok Voice capabilities are available now.

New Homes Are Now $40K Cheaper Than Existing Homes

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (761 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Upcoming-construction homes are less expensive than existing ones, and the difference has never been larger, the National Association of Home Builders has found.
  • According to recent reports, last month's NAHB/Wells Fargo Cost of Housing Index found the median upcoming-home price is $393,300, compared to a median-priced existing home, which comes to $432,900 in the third quarter of 2026.
  • Builders, struggling to find buyers, are digging deeper to offer incentives on fresh homes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upcoming-construction homes are less expensive than existing ones, and the difference has never been larger, the National Association of Home Builders has found.

According to recent reports, last month's NAHB/Wells Fargo Cost of Housing Index found the median upcoming-home price is $393,300, compared to a median-priced existing home, which comes to $432,900 in the third quarter of 2026. That's the largest difference between new- and existing-home prices in the history of NAHB's tracking, Chairman Bill Owens said.

Builders, struggling to find buyers, are digging deeper to offer incentives on fresh homes. The National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index plunged to a 14-year low last week. Many of the nation's major homebuilders have reported large year-over-year declines in revenue. But housing starts continue apace, showing some hope for the market long term.

“Builders are working with buyers to make new homes more affordable and appealing in a tough market, yet the latest CHI data show housing costs still overburden families,” NAHB Chief Economist Robert Dietz remarked in a statement.

In a recent development, A typical family would have to pay 36% of their income for a median-priced existing home. They'd need 33% of their income for a latest home, a drop of 1% from the second quarter. And that accounts for a $17,000 drop in the median new-home price in the second quarter, when it was $434,900, NAHB found.

“As builders contend with rising construction costs, tighter lending standards and persistent labor shortages, policymakers should remove regulatory obstacles, enact permitting reform and create a stronger business environment that enables builders to produce more attainable, affordable homes,” Dietz stated.

Housing costs across the board are rising. Owners are also struggling to manage insurance costs, HOA fees, and utilities.

NAHB's data shows that the San Jose, CA, area is the most cost-burdened market in the third quarter, and 79% of a typical family's income is needed to make a mortgage payment on an existing home. Honolulu, San Diego, San Fransisco, and Barnstable Town, MA, follow. All are above 60%.

Meanwhile, the least cost-burdened market is Decatur, IL, where 17% of a typical family's income is needed to make a mortgage payment on an existing home. Elmira, NY, Peoria, IL, Wichita Falls, TX, and Springfield, IL, all also sit under 20%.

NAHB studied 175 markets and found that, in 95 of them, the typical family is cost-burdened, meaning they spend more than 31% of their income on a median-priced existing home. Eight of those markets are severely cost-burdened, where they pay more than 50%.

According to recent reports, owens remarked that price cuts and incentives are improving affordability. But the nation needs more pro-building laws to solve the underlying problem.

According to recent reports, "According to our latest survey, 43% cut prices in October—the highest share since 2020—and 65% offered sales incentives," Owens said. "But policymakers must do more to reduce red tape, address labor shortages, and fix supply chains so builders can expand the nation’s housing supply.”.

Part of the story is that it's a rough housing market all around.

It has been revealed that the average rate on 30-year fixed home loans jumped to 7.28% last week, up from 7.11% recorded the week before and 6.26% last year, according to Freddie Mac. Pending home sales fell to a record low in October, and existing-home sales hit their lowest level since 2010.

It has been revealed that but part of the story is also how builders have changed up their business. The latest Realtor.com® quarterly construction insights report finds that existing homes are more expensive than upcoming ones based on the price per square foot: $218 for new homes, $219 for existing ones.

Realtor.com senior economist Joel Berner writes that this month's upcoming-construction data points to builders expecting tough conditions to continue.

"Builders are dealing with a litany of obstacles to selling homes, whether it’s rising costs of land, labor, and materials, high financing costs, or weak buyer demand," Berner states. "This month’s data shows them slowing down activity at the top of their funnel, which will result in slower months of starts and completions later on.".

Tristan Navera is a senior reporter on housing policy, covering trends and solutions in the housing market from Washington, DC. He was previously a senior reporter at Bloomberg Law, and before that covered real estate for the Washington Business Journal. Earlier in his career, he spent a decade reporting on business and real estate in Dayton and Columbus, OH. A Cincinnati native, he holds a journalism degree from Ohio University.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Manhattan luxury market has had a banner year despite the pied-à-terre tax and the recent stock market correction.
  • Trophy properties—those priced $10 million and above—made up half the contracts signed last week, leading the luxury market into the second biggest year in two decades, according to Olshan Realty.
  • 22, an impressive 294 contracts were signed at $10 million and above, not far off the peak year of 2021, when 400 were signed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Manhattan luxury market has had a banner year despite the pied-à-terre tax and the recent stock market correction.

Trophy properties—those priced $10 million and above—made up half the contracts signed last week, leading the luxury market into the second biggest year in two decades, according to Olshan Realty.

In a recent development, as of Nov. 22, an impressive 294 contracts were signed at $10 million and above, not far off the peak year of 2021, when 400 were signed. The average asking price for last week was $10.5 million, and properties were moving with a fairly low 5% average discount.

Corcoran's Deborah Grubman, who co-listed last week's most expensive sale—a $28.75 million triplex in the Pritzker Prize–winning Richard Meier building in the West Village—indicates that the luxury market normally shows signs of slowing down around the Thanksgiving holiday. But not this year.

"Upcoming York is still a very desirable destination for people of wealth," she tells Realtor.com®.

According to recent reports, the glass triplex at 176 Perry St.—one of the city's most coveted blocks—was owned by Broadway and movie star Hugh Jackman. The condo, built in 2001, had been on and off the market since June 2022, and at one point was priced at $39 million.

Jackman and his ex-wife, Deborra-Lee Furness, purchased the 11,000-square-foot minimalist abode for $21 million in 2008. Spanning the eighth, ninth and 10th floors, it is "one of the most dramatic apartments in Manhattan," the listing states.

According to recent reports, the full-service condominium comes with sweeping views of the river and Hudson River Park and is within walking distance of The High Line, Little Island, the Meatpacking District, Bleecker Steet, and the Whitney Museum. Jean-Georges Vongerichten's Perry Street Restaurant is on its ground floor.

The Richard Meier building, one of the first ultraluxe buildings that far west, helped change the face of the once-gritty area.

Recent findings suggest that "It was the first 'star-chitect' building in the West Village on the waterfront," says the broker. "It was groundbreaking in terms of luxury. At the time, people stated, 'Who is going to live in the highway?' It predated all that green space.".

While it took Jackman about five years to unload the property, Grubman says that the West Village—and Perry Street, which stretches from Greenwich Avenue to the river—remains in high demand.

Sources indicate that "It's a street that's got lots of charm and history," she notes. "The West Village is out of central casting. You still have the charm of the small townhouses and tree-lined streets.

"The only thing that's really changed a lot is the price point.".

Industry observers note that michelle Griffith of Douglas Elliman represented the buyer of one of the year's top sales: a $16.5 million, 3,855-square-foot condo in the Waldorf Astoria Residences at 301 Park Ave. in Midtown.

The luxury broker says her trophy property sales for 2026 are on track to beat her previous best year, which was 2021.

That year, when 400 ultraluxe contracts were signed, those who weren't fleeing lockdowns were shelling out for multimillion-dollar properties, spurred on by historically low interest rates in the 2% to 4% range.

Recent findings suggest that today, with higher rates hovering around 7%, there are plenty of cash-flush buyers snapping up ultraluxe homes. (Some still prefer 7% mortgage rates to pulling their money out of more lucrative investments.).

It has been revealed that "The phrase that sums up 2026 for me is 'bidding wars,'" the broker tells Realtor.com. "This year will go down as my best year.".

She attributes the surging high-end market to a couple of factors: tight inventory pushing up prices and sparking intense competition, and the "insanely high and insanely competitive" rental market, with rents double or triple what they were just a few years ago.

According to Realtor.com, a three-bedroom-plus in Manhattan has a median monthly rent of $5,375, an increase of 35.6% over the past seven years, requiring a household to earn $215,000 a year just to stay afloat with rent.

However, those who want a luxury three-bedroom-plus abode in a trendy neighborhood can shell out significantly more. Griffith says that a few years ago, a large luxury dwelling in an area like Tribeca could cost around $19,000 a month. But now?

"It would work itself up close to $30,000," she says. "So those people are saying, 'Do I want to spend $30,000 a month or should I pivot and think about buying something? How much am I going to overspend before I say, 'OK, let me buy'?".

Combine stratospheric rents with "inventory levels down across the board," and prices have skyrocketed.

"If you have something good in the West Village, in Tribeca, on the Upper East Side, it is likely going to trade itself up in a bidding war," says the agent.

When dream turnkey apartments began to disappear from listings, buyers became more willing to take on projects, resulting in a stronger-than-normal luxury co-op market. In general, co-ops are much older—and cheaper—than condos.

While the week ending Nov. 22 saw luxury condos outpace co-ops 18-4, there have been several weeks during 2026 when that gap was considerably narrower—and one week in June when co-ops won out.

Recent findings suggest that "These are places that might require several million dollars to renovate," says Griffith. "And now that market too is getting absorbed.".

She notes those who didn't leave the city during the COVID-19 pandemic—fleeing to Westchester, Connecticut, or Florida—are the die-hards who are committed to the city long term. And they are the ones out there bidding up and buying.

Especially relevant are families whose children are deep in the school system.

"They're putting down roots for a minimum of 10 to 15 years," she says.

It has been revealed that despite her banner year, Griffith indicates she isn't planning a celebration just yet. Next year could be a different story as the pied-à-terre surcharge ramps up to replace Department of Finance valuations with significantly higher "fair market" valuations for 2029.

"This year was an emotional journey," she says. "There were many bidding wars we won, but also many we lost. I'm the type who focuses more on, 'What are the deals that we lost?'".

Industry observers note that the second-highest contract of the week was a $25 million sponsor duplex penthouse at 133 E. 73rd St. Listing agency Modlin Group did not return a request for more information.

The Single Asset Vault amendment on the XRP Ledger is getting closer to activation on the mainnet as validator support builds for the network’s preparation to enable better DeFi functionality.

According to data from XRPScan, the SingleAssetVault amendment, or XLS-65, has received yes votes from 25 of 35 trusted validators, right now standing at 71.43% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of 35 votes (29) to start its 14-day countdown to activation. That means it needs four more votes to get there and could reach the magic number before the end of 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the XRP Ledger’s amendment process requires a proposed amendment to be approved by more than 80% of trusted validators for 14 days before it is implemented. Validator support may shift during this time, and if the required 80% threshold is lost, activation may be delayed.

According to recent reports, the Single Asset Vault amendment creates a structure for aggregating assets from multiple depositors and is intended to be used with the on-chain Lending Protocol. The amendment introduces a Vault object that defines the state of a tokenized vault, and the Vault entry is one of the ledger entry types it provides.

In a recent development, the Vault object holds crucial information such as available assets, shares, total value, and other relevant information. Users can create a Vault object with the VaultCreate transaction; the Vault object is tracked in an Owner Directory owned by the Vault Owner account.

The XRP Ledger lending amendment has gained additional yes votes. According to XRPScan, the LendingProtocolV1_1 amendment, also known as XLS-66, has received 24 yes votes out of 35 trusted validators, meaning it has 68.57% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of the 35 votes (29) to trigger a 14-day activation countdown.

This implies that there are five votes left for it to reach this threshold, with the possibility of it securing the required number of votes before the end of 2026 as well.

According to XRP enthusiasts, LendingProtocolV1_1 represents the biggest amendment for unlocking capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger and is anticipated by institutional and retail users.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Although XRP has achieved a sharp price rally after the severe price correction seen in the past months, its recent recovery has yet to influence the performance of its ETF market.
  • Latest data from SoSoValue highlights that momentum across the XRP ETF market has remained slow as the funds have continued to post massive withdrawals during each trading session in recent days.
  • Data reveals that the XRP ETFs managed by Canary Capital and Grayscale recorded combined withdrawals of $6.14 million during their latest trading session on November 17.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although XRP has achieved a sharp price rally after the severe price correction seen in the past months, its recent recovery has yet to influence the performance of its ETF market.

Latest data from SoSoValue highlights that momentum across the XRP ETF market has remained slow as the funds have continued to post massive withdrawals during each trading session in recent days.

Data reveals that the XRP ETFs managed by Canary Capital and Grayscale recorded combined withdrawals of $6.14 million during their latest trading session on November 17.

This also represents the total daily net outflows recorded on that day as only the two funds were active while the rest of the XRP ETF products remained muted with zero participation from investors.

While this means that investors have continued to withdraw their funds despite XRP attempting to reclaim the $1 price level, Canary Capital's XRP ETF saw the highest withdrawal of the day.

Notably, the fund recorded over 5 million XRP, worth about $5.01 million, in daily outflows, while Grayscale's XRP ETF followed with just $1.12 million in outflows.

Although Bitwise did not record any inflow or outflow on this day, the firm still stands as XRP’s biggest ETF manager as it controls over $392.64 million in net assets as of this date.

Despite its dominance in the XRP ETF market, Bitwise has remained muted all week, showing zero daily participation since November 9, when it posted its highest-ever daily outflow of $9.40 million.

  • The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department and the Malibu/Lost Hills Sheriff’s Station responded to a 911 call at the property in the early hours of Nov.
  • According to recent reports, officials told People that they arrived to discover a "structure fire" at the couple's Calabasas home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith's $42 million Los Angeles property went up in flames after their shed caught fire.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department and the Malibu/Lost Hills Sheriff’s Station responded to a 911 call at the property in the early hours of Nov. 23.

According to recent reports, officials told People that they arrived to discover a "structure fire" at the couple's Calabasas home. They added that no one was hurt.

“It appears a shed caught fire, and the cause is believed to be accidental,” the statement from the sheriff's department revealed.

In audio from the 911 call obtained from Page Six, firefighters can be heard saying, "We do have a shed on fire with no spread to the brush.".

An emergency personnel noted that they were already "on scene," and then another firefighter explained that the fire had been "downgraded to a structure.".

The couple's Calabasas property serves as their primary residence. Set on 150 acres, the estate—which they began working on in 1997, the same year they tied the knot—features high-end amenities, including a basketball court, a tennis court, and a massive swimming pool.

The property was designed by architect Stephen Samuelson, who teamed up with Smith and Pinkett Smith in 1997, after they were inspired by the work he had done on the home of Carol Burnett, according to Architectural Digest.

However, it was to be a labor of love for the couple—who had to wait four years to secure the permits to begin construction on their dream home. It would sit at the center of an enormous property that they had amassed over time by buying up adjacent plots of land as they became available.

In the end, Smith and Pinkett Smith created an idyllic Mediterranean-inspired sanctuary for their family, boasting all manner of luxury from a meditation lounge and a recording studio to a sunken trampoline.

Recent findings suggest that it was previously believed that Smith and Pinkett Smith were living apart, with the actress revealing during a previous "Today" interview that she had moved into a new abode in the Los Angeles area. She did not reveal any other details about the property.

The fire comes after Smith, 58, and Pinkett Smith, 55, were spotted in a rare outing alongside their children, Jaden, 28, and Willow, 26.

Last year, the couple put one of their many homes on the market for the relatively low price of $2 million—amid rampant speculation over the state of their marriage.

Many fans have been questioning the status of their relationship since 2022, when Smith infamously slapped Chris Rock across the face during the Oscars ceremony after the comedian made a joke about Pinkett Smith's hair.

Then, just over a year later, Pinkett Smith sensationally revealed during an interview on the "Today" show that she and Smith had been living "completely separate lives" since 2016, despite insisting that they had no aims to legally divorce.

In the two years since that candid confession, questions have continued to be swirl about the truth of their relationship, with Smith sending the rumor mill into overdrive again in February when he put on a very raunchy display with singer India Martínez during an on-stage performance of their song, "First Love.".

Following that public display, the "Men In Black" actor pushed forward a new album, titled "Based on a True Story," marking the first time he has launched a new record in years.

According to Smith, the album is the result of "self-examination" that began after the Oscars incident, which saw the actor banned from all academy events for 10 years.

"I’ve taken the last couple of years to really do a deep dive on the parts of me that may or may not been in that level of certainty and asking those deep scary internal questions," he told the Associated Press.

Industry observers note that "It really is the result of my initial self-examination. Every song is about some part of myself that I discovered or wanted to explore, something I wanted to share. It’s the most full musical offering that I’ve ever created.".

AI agents leaked confidential data in 87 of 100 test runs, Cyberhaven finds

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A newly introduced report out today from data security firm Cyberhaven Inc.
  • The report from Cyberhaven Labs, the tech giant’s research arm, is based on a test in which agents built on five different AI models were given an ordinary marketing task: Write a six-month product report for a company blog, cite the numbers and then publish it.
  • The models tested included three open-weight models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8, along with two closed models in the form of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Sonnet 5.5 and OpenAI Group PBC’s GPT-6.1 Terra.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

According to recent reports, A newly introduced report out today from data security firm Cyberhaven Inc. finds that artificial intelligence agents will leak confidential company data if doing so helps them get the job done, even after noting that it’s confidential.

The report from Cyberhaven Labs, the tech giant’s research arm, is based on a test in which agents built on five different AI models were given an ordinary marketing task: Write a six-month product report for a company blog, cite the numbers and then publish it.

The models tested included three open-weight models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8, along with two closed models in the form of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Sonnet 5.5 and OpenAI Group PBC’s GPT-6.1 Terra.

Confidential data was found to have leaked in 57 of the 60 runs involving the open-weight models, which were also the worst offenders when it came to sharing entire documents. In 16 of those runs, a whole confidential file was made public. In all 16 cases, the agent had flagged the risk in its reasoning before going ahead and doing it anyway. Kimi K3 noted in one run that public links to the board review would expose sensitive data to anyone, calling it “a real-world judgment call” before creating the links regardless.

It was a different story for Anthropic and OpenAI’s models, which flagged confidentiality to the user before publishing in 38 of their 40 runs. Claude did not share a single file in any of its runs, and GPT shared files in only three, each time after first asking for the go-ahead.

In Cyberhaven’s words, the closed models guarded “the container, not the contents.” Any security tool keeping watch over files alone would have missed the leaks entirely.

Nor can most of the leaks be put down to the user giving the green light. The user had been scripted to tell the agents to use their own judgment if asked, but 69 of the 87 leaking runs had already leaked data before the user replied or included material the agent never asked about.

According to recent reports, as for what companies should do about it, Cyberhaven suggests checking what an agent is doing at the moment it shares or publishes something. According to the report, a figure copied from a board review “is still board data,” so content derived from sensitive files should be tracked as well.

The study, which tested a single scenario at one fictional tech giant with a scripted user, is still undergoing a human audit of its results.

It has been revealed that earlier this month, Cyberhaven debuted Agentic Data Security, a product said to track data from its source through every step an agent takes with it. The manufacturer did not use the product in the study.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, asset manager Bitwise has filed an S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a spot Zcash (ZEC) exchange-traded fund. The document appeared in the SEC's database on Nov. 17, 2026. On Wednesday, ZEC rose to $975 before it pulled back to around $927.

Zcash is often called a "more secret" version of Bitcoin. According to the S-1, the Zcash network supports two types of transactions, and the "shielded" ones use a form of zero-knowledge cryptography known as zk-SNARKs. Holders of shielded Zcash "may selectively disclose transaction information to third parties," the filing says.

Bitwise's fund will not use this feature. "The Trust does not engage in shielded transactions in connection with its activities," according to the document.

Recent findings suggest that the shares are expected to list on the Dallas-based Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) under the ticker ZEC. According to the S-1, Coinbase Custody Trust Company will act as the Zcash custodian, and BNY Mellon will serve as the cash custodian. Bitwise also wrote that "the Trust will not stake or otherwise seek to derive additional Zcash from its holdings." The sponsor fee in the filing is listed as "0.___% per annum.".

In the risk section of the S-1, Bitwise wrote that "a number of digital asset trading platforms have delisted Zcash, restricted trading in Zcash or declined to support Zcash." According to the filing, many of these platforms cited regulatory or compliance concerns.

According to recent reports, the platforms that still support Zcash "do so only with respect to transparent addresses and do not permit deposits or withdrawals to or from shielded addresses," the document indicates. Bitwise also pointed to latest EU rules that take effect on July 10, 2027. According to the S-1, the rules will "prohibit credit institutions, financial institutions and crypto-asset service providers in the European Union" from keeping accounts in such assets.

Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan named Zcash one of his top three assets for the decade in September, alongside Bitcoin and tokenization projects. Three days before the S-1 filing, he called ZEC a "golden mean" between open Bitcoin and anonymous Monero in an interview.

Grayscale's Zcash fund (ZCSH) has traded on NYSE Arca since August 2026, and the Winklevoss brothers filed for their own Zcash ETF on Nasdaq in October. ZCSH held $496.79 million as of the Nov. 17 close, according to SoSoValue. The fund has attracted $168.76 million in net inflows since its launch, and it recorded no inflows on Nov. 17, when Bitwise filed its S-1.

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, for three years, U.S.
  • The median home-sale price declined 0.4% year over year to $388,634 in October.
  • With the total number of homes for sale at its highest level since early 2020 and demand cooling, homebuyers’ negotiating power keeps increasing–and that’s finally showing up in sale prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for three years, U.S. home-sale prices rose from a year earlier every single month, even as mortgage rates climbed and would-be buyers pulled back. That streak has ended.

The median home-sale price declined 0.4% year over year to $388,634 in October. That’s  the first decline since May 2023 and a sharp slowdown from the 2.5% gain just two months earlier. With Americans’ wages growing about 4% year over year, even a slight dip in prices can improve affordability. Sale prices have risen nearly every single month for the last 13 years; the only exception was a handful of months in 2023.

With the total number of homes for sale at its highest level since early 2020 and demand cooling, homebuyers’ negotiating power keeps increasing–and that’s finally showing up in sale prices.

Home-sale prices fell nationwide, but they rose in more than half of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas. San Francisco led the nation by a wide margin, with the median sale price rising 16.8% year over year. That’s the biggest increase since 2018. Next comes Fresh Brunswick, NJ, with a 7.7% gain. Two other NYC-area metros also had price increases ranking in the top six; the median sale price rose 4.4% in both New York City and Nassau County.

Industry observers note that in San Francisco, AI wealth is fueling competition for scarce inventory; active listings were down 7% from a year earlier. In the Upcoming York City area, years of limited homebuilding have left buyers competing for relatively few homes in a region with a strong job market.

Industry observers note that home-sale prices fell most in Austin, TX, where they declined 6.5% year over year. It’s followed by Seattle (-5.1%) and Nashville, TN (-4.9%). Austin and Nashville are among the biggest buyer’s markets in the U.S., and Seattle’s shaky tech job market is curbing demand.

Recent findings suggest that national sale prices are losing steam because fewer Americans can afford to buy a home. U.S. pending home sales fell 3.6% from a month earlier in October on a seasonally adjusted basis to their lowest level since 2013, with the exception of April 2020.

This is a real-time indicator of the state of the housing market; fewer homes went under contract in October largely because mortgage rates averaged 7.33%, a three-year high and up from 6.86% the month before.

Sources indicate that all figures in this report are seasonally adjusted, with the exception of median sale price data and mortgage rate data. See a more detailed methodology here and view an interactive dashboard here.

According to recent reports, “It’s a buyer’s market, but not many people can afford to buy,” noted Chen Zhao, Redfin’s head of economics. “That could start to shift a bit, now that sale prices are closer to reflecting the shape of the market. House hunters in most of the country should know that the price they see on a listing may very well be a starting point; they should try offering below the asking price, and negotiating for closing costs, repairs and maybe even mortgage-rate buydowns. If you can’t get the price or monthly payment you want on one house, move on to the next one–with a significant pool of inventory sitting on the market, buyers can afford to be picky.”.

Pending home sales declined in all of the most populous U.S. metros. That’s the second month in a row that has happened; before September, the last time was three years earlier.

The biggest declines were in Seattle and San Diego, both places where pending sales fell more than 20% year over year. Those West Coast metros are some of the priciest in the U.S., so 7%-plus mortgages hit house hunters’ monthly payments there hard. In Seattle, an uncertain local job market is also curbing demand.

Sources indicate that closed home sales fell to their lowest level in nearly 3 years. They declined 2.1% month over month in October to their lowest level since December 2023; before that, the last time sales dropped that low was 2014. Many of the deals that closed last month went under contract in August and September, when rates were already climbing and economic uncertainty was deterring a lot of house hunters.

With homebuying demand falling, supply is building. The total number of homes for sale rose 0.9% from September to its highest level since early 2020; that’s the biggest monthly gain since May 2025.

More supply gives buyers more homes to choose from and more leverage:.

“Buyers are nervous about rates, the economy, and everything they’re seeing in the news– so they need the house and the price to line up perfectly before they’ll make an offer,” mentioned Callie Kimmel, a Redfin Premier agent in Philadelphia. “I’m advising sellers to price just below current market value from day one–and not comps from six months ago, but homes that are listed right now. Otherwise, the home is likely to end up sitting on the market for a bit and selling for less than they hoped. There are a few exceptions: Move-in ready homes in the most desirable neighborhoods are still competitive; in those cases, sellers have the upper hand.”.

While total housing supply is growing, fewer sellers are adding new inventory to the pool. New listings of homes for sale fell 1% month over month to the lowest level in more than two years. Would-be sellers are pulling back as homebuying demand slows and sale prices lose steam.

  • The foundation’s self-assessment was independently verified by the blockchain security firm CertiK on the responses and evidence submitted around the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.
  • The independent attestation report was released on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP Ledger (XRPL) has marked a significant step in its journey to institutional adoption by becoming the first public permissionless layer-1 blockchain to see its principles of Architecture and Resiliency independently verified by the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

The foundation’s self-assessment was independently verified by the blockchain security firm CertiK on the responses and evidence submitted around the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

The independent attestation report was released on Nov. 13, further strengthening the assertion of XRP Ledger's compliance with institutional financial infrastructure requirements.

This comes at a time when banks and asset managers are increasingly considering blockchain technology to enable tokenization of deposits, stablecoins, investment funds and other financial instruments.

The Global Layer One initiative is a collaborative effort between prominent financial institutions and policymakers to set standards for digital financial infrastructure.

Its main goal is to make cross-border transactions for tokenised assets seamless while ensuring that blockchain networks adhere to internationally expected standards for financial market infrastructure.

The GL1 Market Infrastructure Toolkit assesses blockchain networks for adherence to 10 principles, including governance, legal foundation, settlement finality, architecture, operational resiliency, access, interoperability, and privacy.

Interestingly, XRPLF self-assessed XRPL for all 10 principles.

CertiK independently verified it only for the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

XRPLF also provided details on how requirements specific to private/permissioned networks are addressed by managing related risks for XRPL’s decentralized nature, open-source governance model, and protocol amendments.

XRP Ledger Foundation executive director Brett Mollin emphasized the need to give financial institutions tangible evidence instead of pitching ideas.

Mollin added that independent attestation from CertiK also gives financial institutions more confidence while vetting the network.

It does not mean that XRPL meets all the standards mentioned in the toolkit completely.

The XRP Ledger Foundation will continue to update its assessment in line with the development of GL1 principles and XRPL protocol amendments that are activated.

Nonetheless, it's another step towards XRPL's bid to be a possible infrastructure for regulated financial institutions looking for blockchain-based settlement and tokenization.

The Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) on Nov. 18 with seven recommendations on the draft documents CP26/36 and GC26/7. Three of them concern CP26/36, and four concern GC26/7. The letter was signed by HPC chief executive Jake Chervinsky.

The UK's newly introduced crypto regime will start to apply on Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA opened its window for crypto license applications on Sept. 30, 2026, and the window will close on Feb. 28, 2027.

According to the letter, "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity." HPC argued that attaching obligations to a person who could not discharge them "would offer consumers no additional protection.".

In the letter, HPC also compared public blockchains with the internet. "Like a public blockchain, the internet depends on protocols that identifiable persons maintain and upgrade over time," the group wrote.

HPC asked the FCA to assess each participant in a blockchain network separately. Proprietary traders and market makers "supply much of the liquidity on which order books depend," the group wrote. HPC also asked the regulator to describe compliance requirements as outcomes and to hold regulated firms accountable for them.

On Aug. 24, HPC urged the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to harmonize their rules for perpetual contracts. The group argued that such products should be classified by their economic structure. According to HPC, a harmonized framework would let exchanges compete on "execution quality and liquidity.".

Industry observers note that on Sept. 30, HPC sent its response to the European Union's review of the MiCA rules. In it, the group asked the EU to treat crypto perpetual futures as derivatives under MiFID II. "Clarity in application, rather than new legislation, is what would assist in regulating perpetual futures," HPC wrote at the time.

Chervinsky previously served as chief policy officer at the Blockchain Association and as chief legal officer at the crypto venture firm Variant.

Why an Uninsulated Garage Can Wreak Havoc on Your Home This Winter

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (568 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An uninsulated garage might seem like no big deal, but come the winter months, it can do more harm than good.
  • In fact, when a garage lacks proper insulation during the colder months, frozen pipes, heat loss, and damaged items are bound to arise.
  • Fortunately, insulation solutions and preventive measures can help you avoid these concerns while protecting your garage, your car, and your home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An uninsulated garage might seem like no big deal, but come the winter months, it can do more harm than good.

In fact, when a garage lacks proper insulation during the colder months, frozen pipes, heat loss, and damaged items are bound to arise.

Fortunately, insulation solutions and preventive measures can help you avoid these concerns while protecting your garage, your car, and your home.

It has been revealed that an uninsulated garage in the winter months can cause a chain reaction of concerns to the home itself. One of the most common risks is frozen pipes.

“When the plumbing or water lines located in the garage get exposed to below-freezing temps, they may freeze and cause water damage,” explains Chris Boyle, in-house repair tech at Parts Town Home and Fix.com in Nova Scotia.

Additionally, improperly insulated garages can prompt heat loss throughout the entire home.

It has been revealed that “Many poorly insulated garages share foundations with homes. As a result, cold air may circulate through the living spaces and force families to turn up their heating systems,” indicates Boyle.

Not only does this put a strain on HVAC systems, it can also drive up monthly heating bills.

Plus, poor insulation may damage items stored in the garage, particularly car batteries, which can lose charge or fail completely.

So, how do you know for sure whether your garage is insulated?

On a cold day, compare the temperature inside your garage to the outside.

If your garage feels as cold as the outdoors, or if the rooms adjacent to it are always noticeably colder in the winter, there’s a good chance it’s not insulated.

“You can also inspect the walls and ceiling for visible insulation. On the garage door, thin or hollow panels usually indicate a lack of insulation, while thicker panels often mean insulating material is present,” explains Paul Sharpe, owner at Surfside Garage Doors in Toms River, NJ.

Once you determine you have an uninsulated garage, here are several tips to keep on your radar.

For a faster, practical insulation solution, seal any of the bottom gaps under your garage door with rubber weatherstripping.

“If your budget and resources allow, however, the most effective way to retain heat in your garage is to insulate all the walls with fiberglass insulation,” notes Chris Hunter, director of customer relations at ServiceTitan in Glendale, CA.

Regardless of your choice, these solutions will help decrease your energy bill and create a more comfortable environment.

Industry observers note that since the garage door is the largest opening in your home, investing in an insulated garage door may be worthwhile. Entry-level insulated doors typically provide an R-value between 6 and 9, while higher-end models can reach R-values of around 20.

“The higher the R-value, the higher the insulation capabilities and less heat loss that will occur,” explains Sharpe.

You don’t have to expose your valuables to the risks of an uninsulated garage.

“To avoid damaging your items in the garage during winter, you may either elevate them or bring them inside your insulated home,” notes Tamer Sayed, licensed HVAC technician and the owner-operator of Tamas Mechanical in Mississauga, Ontario.

Before the winter begins (or even after, if you missed the boat), consult an HVAC professional for an insulation evaluation. The pro can determine whether your garage is properly safeguarded for the season and recommend the best next steps.

Engel & Völkers is headed to Aruba, where it prepares to open a shop in April 2027, and Realty of America reached California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 of her Team Z Realty agents in San Diego.

“Aruba is a compelling addition to the network’s growing presence in the Caribbean,” Stuart Siegel, president and CEO of Engel & Völkers Americas, mentioned in a statement.

Realty of America entered California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 Team Z Realty agent partners in San Diego. Agent-owned ROA, founded in September 2024, says it has more than 3,900 agents across 26 markets.

“People around me may see what I am giving up, but I see what I am making room for,” Ulloa remarked in a statement.

Rene Carpena and Dana Carpena moved Florida’s 1st Choice Realty, their independent Greater Tampa Bay brokerage, to eXp Realty, where it now operates as 1st Choice Collective. The group brings more than 70 agents and support staff and recorded more than 325 transactions and $60 million in sales volume in 2025, according to the organization.

In a recent development, jon Bowling also brought his 17-person team in Mason, Ohio, to eXp after 20 years with RE/MAX. eXp Realty is the core subsidiary of AGNT Inc.

Industry observers note that baird & Warner added Beyond Properties, a boutique brokerage in Oak Park, Illinois, whose dozen agents will operate as Beyond Properties Group. Owner and designated managing broker Erica Cuneen, who founded the firm almost 20 years ago, will co-lead the group with team leader Cynthia Howe Gajewski. The group joins Baird & Warner’s Oak Park office and keeps its Marion Street location.

“This partnership will allow me to simplify the operational side of the business and spend more time doing what I love, which is focusing on our agents and clients,” Cuneen mentioned in a statement.

Dane Briggs, an Arizona real estate veteran, partnered with Phil Sexton, founder of HomeSmart’s NEXT team, in a leadership role focused on agent workflows and AI integrations. Briggs has worked as a designated broker and title executive, founded referral brokerage Roosted and led expansion initiatives at Homie. He has also served as an Inman Ambassador.

Industry observers note that “Before long, we weren’t just talking about what Phil was building. We were talking about what we could build together,” Briggs stated in a statement.

Ewing spent 13 years at IRES as a projects manager and quality assurance tester before leaving in 2018, and she has more than 20 years of experience in MLS operations and real estate technology.

“Having Samantha return to IRES is an exciting opportunity for our team and the local industry we serve,” CEO Julie Dahl stated in a statement.

Sources indicate that howard Hanna Portside Real Estate Group added Melissa Winter, an agent with nearly 15 years of experience who focuses on first-time homebuyers, to its Massachusetts team in Amesbury. Industry observers note that gold and silver have suffered yet another brutal crash, with approximately $1.4 trillion wiped off their combined market cap in just 24 hours. That's more than the entire market cap of Bitcoin.

Bitcoin, for example, currently has a market cap of roughly $1.26 trillion as of Wednesday, Nov. 18.

According to recent reports, gold saw a brutal drop of roughly 3% on Wednesday, Nov. 18, falling to $3,736 per ounce, its lowest price since September 2025, as per Reuters.

The lustrous metal has now shed about one-third of its value from the record high of nearly $5,595 per ounce hit in January.

Silver experienced an even greater decline of 5.3%, dropping to $44.88 per ounce on Wednesday.

Silver is now down by roughly 63% from its all-time high of over $121 in January. So, the crash is devastating for those investors who jumped on the precious metals bandwagon earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, those fears were further exacerbated by Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller suggesting that the central bank may opt for a 50-basis-point rate hike in December or signal a more aggressive tightening program for 2027.

The crash in precious metals has also been accompanied by another major crash in the crypto market.

Bitcoin fell to near $62,000 over the weekend, and it was also underperforming on Nov. 18, dropping to around $62,450 during Wednesday's trading session.

The same macroeconomic factors affecting the prices of gold and silver are also affecting crypto.

Meanwhile, crypto market maker Wintermute warned that Bitcoin could potentially head into the $50,000 range after falling below the 200-week moving average (a key long-term technical indicator).

Renowned economist and longtime Bitcoin critic Peter Schiff has a troubling message regarding the potential fallout from the Federal Reserve's more aggressive approach to fighting inflation.

On Nov. 18, Schiff shared his thoughts on X, suggesting that gold is dropping as people believe the Federal Reserve means business when it comes to fighting inflation.

If the Fed actually delivers on its promise, the financial system could face potentially disastrous consequences, Schiff has warned.

As a result, market participants could see a huge recession that could lead to a financial crisis even worse than the one we saw back in 2008.

#156417. Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1335 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Redfin ↗ Open Full Page

Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1335 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Redfin

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that just three of the 50 most populous U.S.
  • Nassau County, NY was the number-one seller’s market, with 24.7% fewer sellers than buyers.
  • In a recent development, all three seller’s markets became less strong seller’s markets in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that just three of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas were seller’s markets in October. That’s tied for the fewest in records dating back to 2016, matching April 2020, when the pandemic froze the housing market.

Nassau County, NY was the number-one seller’s market, with 24.7% fewer sellers than buyers. The other seller’s markets were Newark, NJ (-14.3%) and Montgomery County, PA (-12.1%).

In a recent development, all three seller’s markets became less strong seller’s markets in October. In Nassau County, there were 28.3% fewer sellers than buyers in September, a bigger gap than October’s 24.7%. Newark’s gap shrunk from 17.6% to 14.3%, and Montgomery County’s shrunk from 20.1% to 12.1%. Milwaukee, which was a seller’s market in September, is now balanced, meaning it doesn’t favor sellers or buyers.

According to recent reports, the seller’s markets are places where limited homebuilding has kept housing supply tight. In the greater New York City area, combine that with strong demand for homes near a major job center, and buyers are competing for homes. Home-sale prices rose an average of 3.3% year over year across the three seller’s markets in October. That’s compared with a 0.3% uptick across all of the buyer’s markets, a sign that in seller’s markets, competition among buyers is pushing up home prices.

Recent findings suggest that “Buyers looking in these pockets of the Northeast should be prepared for a very different experience than buyers elsewhere in the country,” stated Redfin Senior Economist Asad Khan. “They may have less room to negotiate, especially on desirable, move-in-ready homes, and could face multiple-offer situations. If you’re shopping in one of these markets, it’s especially important to know your budget, be ready to act when the right home comes along and avoid getting swept up in a bidding war.”.

Seller’s markets are the exception to a national picture that heavily favors buyers.

Recent findings suggest that nationwide, homebuyers have more negotiating power than at any point in Redfin’s records. There were an estimated 70.5% more home sellers than buyers in the U.S. housing market in October, the biggest gap in records dating back to 2013.

That marks the sixth record-breaking month in a row, and the margin is up from 65.6% in September. The Sun Belt is driving the extreme buyer’s market nationwide, led by huge seller surpluses in Miami, Nashville, TN and Las Vegas.

Sources indicate that when sellers outnumber buyers, buyers typically have more negotiating power because they have options. That’s why a market with a lot more sellers than buyers is considered a buyer’s market. We define a market where there are over 10% more sellers than buyers as a buyer’s market and a market where there are over 10% fewer sellers than buyers as a seller’s market. A market where the gap is plus or minus 10% is considered a balanced market.

We estimated the number of buyers using proprietary Redfin data on the typical time from a buyer’s first tour to close of purchase, and MLS data on active listings and pending sales. The estimated number of sellers in the market is simply the number of active listings in the MLS. These estimates are seasonally adjusted and subject to revision. See a more detailed methodology here and view an interactive dashboard here.

It’s only a buyer’s market for people who can afford to buy. High housing costs and economic jitters have pushed many would-be homebuyers to back off in recent years, creating the imbalance between buyers and sellers we see today.

“A buyer-friendly market can help make homeownership a little more attainable, even if it doesn’t solve the affordability challenges that have kept many people on the sidelines,” Khan said. “Sellers are increasingly competing for buyers’ attention, which can translate into price reductions, concessions and other savings. First-time buyers don’t have equity from a previous home to put toward a purchase, which makes saving for a down payment a big hurdle–but they also don’t have to sell a home before they can buy or give up a low mortgage rate. With a historic buyer’s market and home prices that are finally ticking down after three years of increases, first-time buyers who have been waiting–and can afford today’s costs–may have an opportunity to make a move.”.

The gap between buyers and sellers widened in October because would-be buyers retreated, while sellers continued listing their homes, albeit at a sluggish pace.

According to recent reports, there were an estimated 895,752 homebuyers in the market nationwide in October, the lowest level in records dating back to 2013. That’s down 2% from a month earlier, the sixth straight monthly decline. Mortgage rates averaged 7.33% in October, up from 6.86% in September, which priced out more would-be buyers.

On the flip side, there were an estimated 1,526,984 home sellers in the market, the most since March 2020. That’s up 0.9% month over month.

The number of homes on the market is piling up because many homes are lingering on the market for months without going under contract. Each month, more latest listings are adding to the massive pool of supply.

In a recent development, some homeowners keep listing their houses despite falling demand because many have given up on waiting for lower rates. They may want to sell now because they’re worried prices could decline, and some need to move for a new job, a growing family, or another life change. But many homeowners who don’t need to move have substantial equity and little pressure to sell, so they may hold off on listing.

In a recent development, over 80% of U.S. metro areas, 41 of the 50 Redfin analyzed, are buyer’s markets. That matches September’s record.

According to recent reports, for the third month in a row, Miami and Nashville have the biggest surpluses of sellers over buyers. Miami had 195.8% more sellers than buyers in October, and Nashville had 159.5% more. Las Vegas (149.9%) was third on the list. In the top 13 buyer’s markets, there were more than twice as many sellers as buyers in October. Nearly all are in the Sun Belt; four are in Texas and four are in Florida.

Industry observers note that the Sun Belt, particularly Texas and Florida, is home to some of the nation’s biggest buyer’s markets, partly because of robust homebuilding. Builders are continuing to add upcoming homes even as demand cools, swelling inventory and giving buyers more options and negotiating power.

Demand has cooled largely because rising mortgage rates and stubbornly high home prices are pricing buyers out. In Florida, rising HOA and homeowners insurance costs are exacerbating the affordability squeeze.

Six metros were “balanced” in October, neither buyer’s nor seller’s markets: Chicago (8.1% more sellers than buyers), Boston (7.5%), Providence, RI (7.5%), Fresh Brunswick, NJ (5.6%), Milwaukee (0.6% fewer sellers than buyers) and San Francisco (6.9% fewer).

The surplus of home sellers over buyers grew month over month in 34 of the 41 buyer’s markets in October.

The surplus increased most in Miami, which also has the biggest surplus of sellers over buyers; there were 195.8% more sellers than buyers in October, up from 160.5% the month before. The next-biggest monthly increases were in Las Vegas, where there were 149.9% more sellers than buyers, up from 122.8%, and Nashville (159.5%, up from 134.3%).

House hunters lost negotiating power in seven buyer’s markets. The surplus of sellers over buyers fell from September to October in Fort Worth, TX (91.6%, down from 100%), St. Louis (23.1%, down from 27.1%), Austin (124.8%, down from 128.2%), Dallas (118.6%, down from 120.5%), Jacksonville, FL, Pittsburgh and Los Angeles. All of them remain buyer’s markets.

According to recent reports, as a data journalist at Redfin, Dana Anderson writes about the numbers behind real estate trends.
