Your Customers Just Got an AI Agent. Is Your Business Ready to Talk to Them?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Entrepreneur

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.
  • Right now, companies are interacting with customers who are not giving up, losing their patience after being put on hold or missing what’s in the fine print of the business’s policies.
  • Sources indicate that meta’s Muse and xAI’s Grok Bot are the two getting the most attention right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Right now, companies are interacting with customers who are not giving up, losing their patience after being put on hold or missing what’s in the fine print of the business’s policies. That’s because these customers aren’t humans. They’re personal AI agents acting on behalf of humans.

Sources indicate that meta’s Muse and xAI’s Grok Bot are the two getting the most attention right now. Muse skyrocketed up to number one in the App Store, and Meta’s stock jumped double digits in the same week. Financial markets have been trying to price what these personal agents mean for retail, travel and banking. Massive corporations are already reacting, with Amazon blocking Muse outright and Shopify electing to build Muse its own checkout lane instead.

Sources indicate that there’s a lot of noise right now about what these personal AI agents should and will be allowed to do. The dust has clearly not settled, and some very key questions hang in the air. But make no mistake: This will not be a passing trend or a footnote in the broader story of AI innovation. This is a massive shift in how businesses interact with customers, and the companies that start getting ready for it now are the ones who will be prepared when it arrives at their front door.

From the consumer’s perspective, a personal agent fights the battles they don’t want to, and does so more rigorously than they ever could.

Someone’s flight gets cancelled, and their personal agent can argue with the airline until it gets a credit. Someone points it at subscription services and gets every one to offer a discounted rate. I’ve seen dozens of these examples pile up on social media over the past few weeks, and the pattern is always the same. A task a person would normally decide was not worth the trouble is now getting done anyway, because an agent has no concept of trouble.

It has been revealed that we used to think about bots talking to bots like something that will happen “someday.” It’s happening now. For consumers who don’t want to solve problems through sheer persistence and patience, this is an exciting development. For businesses that have built their customer service programs around interacting with humans, this is a challenge to solve, fast.

According to recent reports, the simple response to this innovation sounds like: “We need our policies to be accurate, because AI will be better at calling us out on them than a human customer.” It goes deeper than that. Every refund policy and guarantee clause has fine print and phrases that are ever so slightly open to interpretation. Personal AI agents can read these policies and find where they bend in ways a human never could.

Industry observers note that and they’ll do this at scale. One customer raising a question and finding a loophole is a cost of doing business. Thousands of agents doing the same thing can overwhelm a business, both financially and operationally.

In a recent development, that kind of volume does not behave like a normal surge in customer support demand. It behaves more like a denial-of-service attack. Nobody debates whether each individual request is legitimate; the volume itself is the problem. The response has to be infrastructural: detecting, filtering, a real system for deciding what gets through. “We will deal with it when it happens” is not a strategy at this scale.

Retail and travel may seem like the industries most vulnerable to risk, but any business with documented policies faces the same exposure. Insurance, financial services, healthcare — wherever a tech giant has put a promise or statement of intent in writing, an agent can find it and act on it.

AI has already carved out a massive role in how businesses interact with customers. Now it’s showing up on the other side of the conversation. Nobody has every single answer for how to prepare for this latest reality, us included. But there are foundational moves worth making now, rather than waiting for the rest of the industry to decide what to do.

Recent findings suggest that first, there’s the question of identity. Most businesses have no reliable way to know whether they are talking to a customer, a customer’s authorized agent or something pretending to be one. That infrastructure needs to be in place before anything else matters.

Second, you need visibility into what is already happening. You need to be able to see how often an agent is showing up in a support queue, what it’s asking for and how often it’s succeeding.

Then there’s the problem of the policies themselves. A traditional review to ensure accuracy is no longer sufficient. Businesses need to audit their policies, line by line, and stress-test every potential ambiguity that could turn into a vulnerability. Find the gaps before an agent does.

According to recent reports, resist the instinct to default to blocking. Throughout history, we’ve seen what happens to companies that try to close a door that’s going to be kicked down regardless. Search engines that tried to wall off the open web lost to the ones that stayed open, and the same pattern is likely to repeat here. Open does not mean undefended. It means building real verification and governance instead of a blanket “no,” even while the rest of the playbook is still being written.

Industry observers note that significant players are picking sides right now, with Amazon blocking personal agents and Shopify building a lane. It’s tempting to treat their moves as a test case, something to monitor from the sidelines until the winds blow in one definitive direction.

In a recent development, that would be a mistake. Sure, the headlines may change in a week; in the case of these specific AI agents and the companies that created them, there may be developments that complicate their rapid surge in the short term. But the shift is happening, and CX organizations can’t be lulled into a reactive posture.

According to recent reports, nobody has built the perfect system for this yet. But the companies spending this period of uncertainty getting their infrastructure ready will be the ones with real footing when the dust settles. Everyone else will still be reading the news, wondering what to do next.

Recent findings suggest that right now, companies are interacting with customers who are not giving up, losing their patience after being put on hold or missing what’s in the fine print of the business’s policies. That’s because these customers aren’t humans. They’re personal AI agents acting on behalf of humans.

Industry observers note that meta’s Muse and xAI’s Grok Bot are the two getting the most attention right now. Muse skyrocketed up to number one in the App Store, and Meta’s stock jumped double digits in the same week. Financial markets have been trying to price what these personal agents mean for retail, travel and banking. Massive corporations are already reacting, with Amazon blocking Muse outright and Shopify electing to build Muse its own checkout lane instead.

There’s a lot of noise right now about what these personal AI agents should and will be allowed to do. The dust has clearly not settled, and some very crucial questions hang in the air. But make no mistake: This will not be a passing trend or a footnote in the broader story of AI innovation. This is a massive shift in how businesses interact with customers, and the companies that start getting ready for it now are the ones who will be prepared when it arrives at their front door.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer and head of its Superintelligence Labs, posted on X on Sunday that “superintelligence is arriving.” He wrote that “the models are clearly going to be intelligent enough to automate all of AI research,” and that “it is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement.” He said the remaining obstacles are “no longer intelligence; they are domain-specific know-how, plumbing, and experimentation.”.

“How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in,” Wang wrote.

Social media erupted over the latest warning from inside the AI thunderdome during a weekend when the AI bubble seemed to finally have popped—the day before it controversially reinflated again. Wang wasn’t even posting about Anthropic’s IPO or Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia—to be followed by his sudden reinstatement on Monday morning.

Industry observers note that he was riffing on just the latest historic math breakthrough with the help of generative AI: the claim by Levent Alpöge, a mathematician on Anthropic’s technical staff, of a proof of the Riemann hypothesis made with Anthropic’s Claude. The 167-year-old problem about the distribution of prime numbers is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s $1 million Millennium Prize problems.

“It is hard to overstate the magnitude of discovery that we have just witnessed,” Wang wrote about the milestone, describing it as completed “with the help of an alien mind that we don’t understand.” He added that building an atomic bomb is “a homework problem compared to the Riemann hypothesis.”.

Wang’s warning came as Meta expects to devote $135 billion to $145 billion to capital expenditures this year, driven largely by AI infrastructure costs.

Wang’s post spread fast. The Next Web counted more than 8 million views in its first half day, and the reaction crossed the usual political lines. Jon Favreau, President Obama’s former director of speechwriting, called it “f—ing madness” and stated the people Americans elected should be doing everything they can to stop the frontier labs “from handing over control of humanity to superintelligent machines.”.

From the right, Megyn Kelly posted: “This is the head of Meta’s superintelligence lab. We’ve had similar warnings from Anthropic, the former head of alignment at OpenAI, not to mention Elon himself at X. How many more do we need until we garner the all-hands-on-deck reaction this deserves?”.

In a recent development, wang argued against fatalism. He wrote that he noticed “a particular form of lazy thinking within the AI industry”: the view that “ASI is inevitable and the only problem to solve is how to do it safely.” He added, “We should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.”.

After the backlash, he wrote, “What I am saying is, this path is not inevitable,” and “leaders and leadership matter more than ever.” He pointed to Meta’s decision to delay the launch of its Muse model for months and to Zuckerberg’s call for most computing power to go toward serving customers rather than toward AI that improves itself.

Zuckerberg made Wang the center of Meta’s AI push in June 2025, when Meta invested $14.3 billion in Wang’s former company, Scale AI, for a 49% stake. In January, Zuckerberg told investors that “this is going to be a massive year for delivering personal superintelligence.” Meta has raised the bottom of its 2026 spending guidance at every quarterly report since, from $115 billion in January to $135 billion in October.

As for the Riemann hypothesis, Anthropic’s Alpöge has said he plans to explain the AI-generated proof in talks and a written account. Until mathematicians read it, the Clay Institute’s $1 million stays unclaimed.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that daily pool data demonstrates Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped.
  • Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.
  • Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Recent findings suggest that daily pool data demonstrates Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

According to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

In a recent development, zecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

In a recent development, across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:.

Together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

Sources indicate that october was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:.

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

Industry observers note that at September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

Industry observers note that the deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

Sources indicate that NU7 does not introduce a new transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable.".

Industry observers note that the coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

The rest of the upgrade is larger:.

Industry observers note that ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

As of ZecStats' latest revision on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

In October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

Sources indicate that small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who proposal to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

In practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. Users need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

It has been revealed that the September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

That has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Industry observers note that every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

In a recent development, the useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 20, 2026 at 9:41 amNovember 20, 2026 at 9:41 am.

A newly introduced baby can be the ultimate anxiety trigger: When will she sleep through the night? What if nursing is a challenge. What is that rash?! Given the countless unknowns, the last thing a parent needs are worries about the quality of the baby’s crib or the chemicals in a pacifier.

But when Karthik Gangiredla was preparing for the birth of his first daughter, he and his wife spent hours trying to figure out which baby products were trustworthy.

“We struggled a lot,” Gangiredla said. “We did a lot of research on what was safe, what’s not.”.

An engineer with roughly 20 years of experience in supply chains and logistics, including roles at Amazon, Flexport and TikTok, Gangiredla found himself on the consumer side of the retail equation, scrutinizing strollers and bottles.

To spare other parents the same headache, he turned that research into Birch, an online marketplace that offers baby product buying guides and assigns each item a TrustScore. Its scoring system draws on certifications, lab reports and recall databases to help parents assess goods ranging from baby wipes to teething toys.

The site provides information on more than 10,000 items across 110 brands, including manufacturing locations, suppliers, certificate numbers and test reports.

Birch has contracts with brands it has checked out, and serves as their merchant of record, meaning if a customer has challenges with a product or wants to return it, Birch handles those steps. It operates fulfillment centers in Los Angeles and Upcoming Jersey.

It has been revealed that gangiredla said the startup flips the e-commerce approach of retail giants, focusing on the shoppers’ needs, not those of the merchant. It does not accept ads or sponsored rankings.

According to recent reports, if you took away the ad revenue for Amazon or TikTok, “the business wouldn’t exist,” Gangiredla stated. “So it’s very difficult for them to approach the problem in a different way.”.

According to recent reports, the platform also offers a gift registry and tools for tracking fetal development during pregnancy, an infant’s nursing and sleep schedules, and other developmental steps. The tools are free for users.

We caught up with Gangiredla, Birch’s CEO and founder, for this edition of GeekWire’s Startup Spotlight.

In 50 words or less, give us your startup’s elevator pitch.

Birch is the trust-first platform for baby and kids products and parenting resources. We research and score products across 50+ safety and quality signals before listing — and stock only what clears the bar — so parents skip the endless research and buy with confidence, from pregnancy through the toddler years.

What problem are you obsessed with solving?

The impossible research burden on latest parents. Every purchase feels like a safety decision, the information is scattered and often unverified, and the stakes feel enormous. We’re obsessed with moving the work of figuring out what’s trustworthy off the parent and onto a system that does it rigorously — and then showing our work.

What surprised you after talking to customers?

In a recent development, how universal the trust problem is. We assumed it would track with income or with first-time parents, but our customers span all 50 states and every kind of household — big metros to small towns. And what they consistently want isn’t more options or a lower price; it’s someone to tell them, credibly, what’s actually worth buying.

How has AI changed the way you build your tech giant?

Recent findings suggest that it’s core, not a feature. Our TrustScore engine evaluates thousands of products across dozens of safety and quality signals in ways a human team our size never could, and the same intelligence powers discovery and personalization. It also lets a very lean team operate like a much larger one — and we now license that engine to other baby and kids brands as a product called Juno.

What’s one thing people misunderstand about your startup?

That “curated” means limited or expensive. Curation isn’t about carrying less for its own sake, or about selling premium — it’s about removing the untrustworthy. In our own data, price and trustworthiness barely correlate; some of the highest-scoring products are among the most affordable. Fewer and better, not fewer and pricier.

What’s the toughest decision you’ve made in the past year?

Turning away brands and revenue. When you’re early, every dollar is tempting — but our entire promise is that everything on Birch has earned its place. Saying no to products and partners that didn’t clear the bar, even when the revenue was real, was hard. It’s also the decision that defines what we are.

What’s the one piece of advice you give to other entrepreneurs?

Earn trust before you try to scale it. It’s slower and less glamorous than chasing growth, but trust compounds and shortcuts don’t. And talk to your customers far earlier, and far more often, than feels comfortable.

We’ll know our organization has made it when….

…a parent’s first instinct, the moment they find out they’re expecting, is to come to Birch — and “did you check the TrustScore?” is just how families talk about buying for their kids.

Anthropic’s 5,300 employees are starting a upcoming week with more money than they could fathom just days ago.

Sources indicate that the manufacturer’s IPO sent its collective employee wealth soaring, putting the average non-founder staff’s estimated fortune at more than $44 million. But for 598 non-founder employees, they now have at least $100 million to their name, according to a report by private-markets investing firm Hill, cited by Reuters.

Recent findings suggest that that means Anthropic has more centimillionaires among its ranks than there are living in the entirety of London, Paris, or Los Angeles. The only cities with more are San Francisco and New York City, according to wealth migration firm Henley & Partners.

Sources indicate that those estimates are based on Anthropic’s $83-per-share IPO price, a level the stock has yet to fall below. By Thursday’s close, shares had climbed to $97.17, putting the collective estimated wealth of Anthropic’s employees and seven cofounders at roughly $433 billion—more wealth than the entire bottom one-third of Americans, according to a viral analysis by Steve Rattner.

While Anthropic shares have since pulled back to around $88—making the total Anthropic staff equity closer to $350 billion—the wealth gains remain substantial.

Anthropic’s rise after being founded in 2021 has been meteoric. But critics have warned that the wealth generated by its rapid growth is also raising questions about who stands to benefit from the AI boom—and who could be left behind.

Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel, who appeared at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum earlier this month, said changes need to be made to the tax code so that so much wealth cannot be preserved among a few people.

According to recent reports, “AI has the potential to create enormous prosperity. But if all that wealth flows to a handful of people at the top while working families struggle to get ahead, we’re not building an economy of the future,” he posted on X. “We’re repeating the mistakes of the past.”.

Hana Ivanhoe, senior manager of private sector campaigns and advocacy at anti-poverty nonprofit Oxfam America, echoed to Fortune that Anthropic’s IPO offers a striking example of how the AI boom could deepen existing economic divides.

“The level of wealth concentration that Anthropic’s IPO has precipitated is obviously jarring, and it’s emblematic of the extreme inequality that already characterizes our economy and is sure to be exacerbated by future IPOs like this one,” she said.

That wealth is being generated amid growing questions about AI’s breakneck pace of development and its potential consequences for the job market—and even humanity itself.

Sources indicate that “It’s not only a problem that these IPOs are making a rich few even richer, it’s that they are getting richer at the expense of everyone else,” Ivanhoe added. “There’s both wealth inequality and inequality of impact at play here.”.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s net worth skyrocketed to some $21 billion with the IPO, but he has also voiced concerns about the consequences of AI driving that wealth.

“The thing to worry about is a level of wealth concentration that will break society,” he wrote in a letter released in January.

In response, Amodei, alongside his fellow six founders, committed to donate 80% of their Anthropic equity to philanthropy—and urged others to be more generous with their giving.

In a recent development, and while Amodei has also called for the AI industry to slow down development amid his own concerns about AI systems going rogue, being used in cyberattacks and bioterrorism, or causing serious economic disruption, Anthropic went through with its IPO, in part, because of a need for more financing to develop AI safely. Competitor OpenAI delayed its IPO until 2027.

Whitney & Co., where he played a role in investments tied to The North Face, Igloo and Herbalife, Peter came out of retirement to become the founder and CEO of WISEcode, an AI-powered food transparency platform that has mapped more than 840,000 products. He’s 70 years old and says he’s never felt more excited about an idea, proving it’s never too late to chase a big idea.

Give us the elevator pitch. What is WISEcode?Basically, we’re trying to solve what I call the food information crisis. We literally don’t know two things: what’s in our food and what it does to us. At WISEcode, we’ve been spending a dozen years or so solving that. We’ve created what we call the Food Genome Project, which is really mapping the entire food system. That information didn’t exist, and now it does.

I eat generally well. But when you turn 50, you enter the kill zone for chronic disease, and chronic disease is 90% of our health issues, and 80% of chronic disease is driven by what we choose to do. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • The price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility.
  • According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is currently facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.
  • According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is currently facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further highlights that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is vital to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

At the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data highlights that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

Latest Update: I Stayed On a Private Island in Fiji. It Pulls Off a Top Travel Trend With a Luxury Twist—Here’s What Any Hospitality Business Can Learn.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Lang Walker, the late Australian billionaire property developer and philanthropist, and his wife, Sue Walker, first saw Yaukuve Levu Island, Kadavu, Fiji, surrounded by the Great Astrolabe Reef, the land was largely overgrown, with the remains of a development that had never been completed.
  • According to recent reports, “We anchored the boat out the front, looked at it and thought what a wonderful place this could be,” Sue Walker recalls.
  • That effort led to Kokomo Private Island, which officially opened in March 2017.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Lang Walker, the late Australian billionaire property developer and philanthropist, and his wife, Sue Walker, first saw Yaukuve Levu Island, Kadavu, Fiji, surrounded by the Great Astrolabe Reef, the land was largely overgrown, with the remains of a development that had never been completed.

According to recent reports, “We anchored the boat out the front, looked at it and thought what a wonderful place this could be,” Sue Walker recalls. “It took eight years and an enormous amount of hard work to bring that vision to life.”.

That effort led to Kokomo Private Island, which officially opened in March 2017.

Today, the property features 21 beachfront villas and five hilltop residences, each with a private pool; three principal dining venues, with more than 80% of herbs and greens sourced from the island’s 5.5-acre organic farm; the Yaukuve Spa Sanctuary with its dedicated fitness center; and no shortage of adventure and cultural activities available to its guests.

My husband and I had a chance to experience the tropical island paradise for ourselves in September. Throughout our stay, we were struck by Kokomo’s sheer natural beauty and how much the luxury hospitality experience was rooted in a genuine sense of place.

Sources indicate that increasingly, hotels and resorts highlighting local character rise to the top of travelers’ wishlists. Nearly three-quarters of luxury travelers won’t pay for accommodations that feel generic, per a report from Preferred Hotels & Resorts, and 77% of travelers prioritize authentic experiences representative of local culture, according to research from Booking.com.

Kokomo serves as a lesson in hospitality excellence — what it takes to succeed in a travel landscape increasingly defined by a desire for authenticity and local character. Here’s how every business can do the same.

Industry observers note that after a long day (or more) of travel, first impressions are key. Guests want to feel at ease and an immediate sense of place. But, sometimes, that’s the straightforward part. Sustaining that genuine warm welcome throughout the stay also matters.

Staff members at Kokomo give it its personality and make guests feel at home, often forming relationships that bring people back year after year, Walker claims.

Additionally, Kokomo has developed a close relationship with the local community, where some staff members are from: supporting local employment, working with neighboring villages, and contributing to education, healthcare and community initiatives.

“Authenticity comes from allowing those relationships and traditions to exist naturally, rather than trying to manufacture an experience for guests,” Walker says. “When someone shares a story about their village, introduces a guest to a local custom or folklore or even simply welcomes them with genuine Fijian hospitality, that’s what stays with people.”.

In a recent development, our arrival and journey to Kokomo was seamless from the first “bula” (Fijian for “hello” and a wish for life and good health). After a 45-minute seaplane ride, we touched down on the crystalline blue waters in front of Kokomo. We were given a salusalu, a traditional garland worn around the neck, and coconut water, and listened to a group of staff members sing traditional Fijian welcome songs.

Sources indicate that that warmth and hospitality extended throughout our time at Kokomo, across the interactions we had with staff and when we visited the nearby Dravuni Village, which is home to a small indigenous Fijian community. We heard traditional songs, learned about their hand-woven crafts, participated in a kava ceremony and toured the village with a staff member who’d grown up there.

The business lesson is this: Lean into what makes a destination special, and the cultural touchstones that define it, for an authentic welcome that extends from the first moment to the last.

Of course, as much as people want to soak up all a destination has to offer, they’ll spend a good portion of their vacation in their accommodations. Ideally, those accommodations capture the destination’s unique characteristics while prioritizing comfort.

From the beginning, the Walkers wanted Kokomo to feel like home, “albeit a rather extraordinary one,” where families could create lifelong memories with the privacy, space and luxury afforded by their own quiet corner of the island.

It has been revealed that “For me, true luxury isn’t about formality,” Walker claims. “It’s about comfort, freedom, being able to enjoy yourself without feeling constrained by the usual expectations of a hotel. Children should be able to run around, explore and have adventures, while their parents and grandparents can relax and enjoy the island in their own way.”.

Recent findings suggest that our one-bedroom beachfront villa, just steps from the ocean, felt sprung from the tropical landscape itself. The high ceilings, neutral stone and wood, and ample windows, the better to display the expansive patio with its private pool and the dazzling ocean view, created an indoor-outdoor flow with understated natural elegance.

When it comes to architecture, interior design, or landscape, embracing what sets the place surrounding it apart from any other, rather than competing with it, helps establish that seamless, one-of-kind experience guests won’t forget.

It has been revealed that whether a guest is a serious gourmet or not, meals will stand out as part of the experience (a three-times-a-day touchpoint). For remote resorts where guests rely solely on the dining on-site, it’s even more critical to deliver elevated, locally-defined experiences.

Early on, the Walkers realized they had access to the best ingredients on their doorstep — fresh seafood and the climate and space to grow much of the island’s own produce — and built their culinary philosophy around that, Walker states.

“A fish caught locally that morning, vegetables picked from the garden, herbs cut just before they’re used,” she explains. “You can’t get much fresher than that. Building and operating a resort in such a remote location comes with enormous logistical challenges, so growing more of our own food and reducing our reliance on imported produce makes sense on many levels.”.

Industry observers note that we had a chance to go on a tour with Kokomo’s executive chef Marty Kindleysides. He gave us an inside look at the island’s farm and hydroponic gardens, which help shape the menus across its restaurants: the Beach Shack on Kokomo’s western beach; Walker D’Plank, featuring Asian-influenced cuisine, near the arrival jetty; and the poolside Kokocabana, highlighting Italian-inspired dishes.

From the beautiful lunch Kindleysides prepared for us with farm-fresh ingredients like squash and kale, to all of the meals we enjoyed at the other dining venues, including a showstopping dinner by Chef Caroline during a curry-themed night at Walker D’Plank, the food was flavorful, intentional and reinforced a singular dining experience.

Guests should never feel like the food where they’re staying is an afterthought; it’s another opportunity — and a very memorable one — to showcase innovation and what makes a setting unique.

At a remote tropical resort like Kokomo, guests have the luxury of a picture-perfect natural setting offering once-in-a-lifetime activities. But striking the balance between making the most of the environment and protecting it is also critical.

According to recent reports, lang was an avid diver for most of his life and immediately recognized the wonder of the Great Astrolabe Reef. The Walkers saw it as their responsibility to look after it, so they set out to help guests experience and understand it.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s something quite powerful about a child helping to plant coral, or a family learning about the individual manta rays that return to our waterways each season,” Walker says. “Suddenly conservation becomes personal. You’re no longer looking at a beautiful reef, rather, you’re beginning to understand how it works and why protecting it matters.”.

We had the opportunity to meet with a marine biologist to learn about the manta rays and conservation efforts. Kokomo has partnered with Manta Project Fiji to research and protect Fiji’s reef manta rays since 2017. More than 500 manta ray sightings were recorded during the most recent monitoring period. We even went to look for them by boat, but unfortunately with it being the tail end of the season, didn’t spot any.

It has been revealed that additionally, the marine biologist led us on a guided coral restoration tour, where we snorkeled over some of the current projects underway. More than 2,000 corals have been transplanted as part of Kokomo’s coral restoration. The island also has six active coral nurseries, which can support more than 10,000 corals per season.

Bringing guests into the very projects that protect the place they’re staying gives them destination-driven, extraordinary experiences while safeguarding them for future generations.

Relaxation means different things to different people, but centralizing spa and wellness options in one place, and melding personalized comfort with distinct ambiance, gives everyone the option to design an ideal routine to reset.

The Walkers wanted to build on the feeling guests have upon arrival — everyday life demands removed by the grandeur of nature — and developed the Yaukuve Spa Sanctuary with that in mind.

According to recent reports, “The gardens, the tropical landscape, the sense of privacy all contribute to the experience,” Walker claims. “I wanted guests to feel that they could completely switch off, even if only for an hour or two. I don’t think wellness needs to be complicated or overly prescriptive. Sometimes the greatest luxury is having the time and space to do what makes you feel good, without the schedule or expectation.”.

It has been revealed that we enjoyed Kokomo’s signature “Pacific Mastery Massage,” which incorporates centuries-old methods from traditional Fijian Bobo, combining variable pressure and rhythmic movement with the preferred oil blend. Before and after the service, we sipped iced hibiscus tea (the flower is often seen in Fijian landscaping) in the garden setting.

Guests will remember how a vacation makes them feel, so making sure they have the option to truly unwind, whatever that looks like for them, is key. Infusing it with a local twist means they won’t forget exactly where they experienced it.

At the end of the stay, as we departed on the one-hour helicopter ride back to the hangar, spotting our villa on the lush island encircled by a shock of turquoise, we came away already nostalgic for the trip, and with a deeper appreciation for Fiji’s natural beauty and vibrant culture.

We would love to return some day (maybe to snorkel with the mantas) — and that’s exactly what the Walkers intended.

“More than anything, I hope guests leave Kokomo feeling they’ve been part of something special,” Walker states. “That they’ve spent quality time with the people they love, experienced the generosity of our Fijian team and discovered a part of the world they’ll always remember. If they leave feeling as though Kokomo is their island home, then we’ve achieved what we set out to do.”.

When Lang Walker, the late Australian billionaire property developer and philanthropist, and his wife, Sue Walker, first saw Yaukuve Levu Island, Kadavu, Fiji, surrounded by the Great Astrolabe Reef, the land was largely overgrown, with the remains of a development that had never been completed.

“We anchored the boat out the front, looked at it and thought what a wonderful place this could be,” Sue Walker recalls. “It took eight years and an enormous amount of hard work to bring that vision to life.”.

That effort led to Kokomo Private Island, which officially opened in March 2017.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Microsoft acquired the popular Wunderlist app in 2015, shut it down in 2020 and told its loyal people that Microsoft To Do would be their new home.
  • Recent findings suggest that microsoft plans to retire the To Do apps on June 30, 2027, moving personal task management for work and school accounts into Planner, its team project-management app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 20, 2026 at 2:06 pmNovember 20, 2026 at 2:08 pm.

Microsoft acquired the popular Wunderlist app in 2015, shut it down in 2020 and told its loyal people that Microsoft To Do would be their new home. Now it’s asking them to switch again.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft plans to retire the To Do apps on June 30, 2027, moving personal task management for work and school accounts into Planner, its team project-management app. Microsoft disclosed the change Wednesday in a long Planner blog post amid the firm’s Ignite announcements, and Windows Latest flagged the change later that day.

It has been revealed that the reaction was swift and mostly unhappy. Tom Warren of The Verge summed it up on X: “Microsoft is killing its great tasks app in favor of its worse tasks app.”.

It has been revealed that that’s not entirely fair to Planner, which is built for a different job. But it captures the gripe: To Do was simple, free and worked across Windows, Mac, iOS, Android and the web, and nothing Microsoft is offering replaces all of that.

For work and school accounts, Microsoft states Planner “will be the destination for managing personal work tasks,” but “existing To Do tasks and lists will not migrate to Planner.” It says it will offer a way to export To Do data before the app shuts down.

Tony Redmond of Office365itpros, who tracks Microsoft 365 closely, cataloged the gaps: no file attachments on private Planner tasks, no equivalent for To Do’s list groups, no transfer of shared-list membership, assignments or permissions, and no native Planner apps for Windows or Mac.

He also noted the irony that Outlook’s old Exchange-based tasks will outlive To Do.

Why Microsoft is doing it: The company noted putting individual and shared work on the same foundation lets it deliver more consistent features, and lets people connect their own tasks to Copilot and other AI agents. A new Planner agent, available with a Copilot add-on license, can take on tasks and generate status reports.

The Register’s Richard Speed put it less charitably, saying Microsoft had slipped the news into “this week’s Ignite AI puffery.”.

Users weigh in: Brad Silverberg, the former Microsoft executive who led Windows 95 development and later became a Seattle venture investor, posted on X that he has used To Do daily, and Wunderlist before it.

“Very disappointed now,” he wrote, adding that he’s looking at TickTick and Todoist.

Similar posts piled up on LinkedIn from Microsoft 365 consultants and everyday users, some of them describing Planner as clunky by comparison.

Patrick Husting, a Seattle-area entrepreneur and software developer whose Ghostwriter add-in brought AI to Microsoft Office before Microsoft announced Microsoft 365 Copilot, offered on LinkedIn to maintain To Do for Microsoft for free.

It has been revealed that rivals smell an opportunity: Competitors wasted no time. TickTick posted a migration guide for To Do refugees. Todoist CEO Amir Salihefendic wrote on LinkedIn that the shutdown was “pretty unexpected” and pointed out that his app has outlasted competitors for 20 years.

The most pointed pitch came from Superlist, which called itself “the natural successor” and noted it already has a tool for importing To Do lists. Wunderlist founder Christian Reber started the tech giant in 2020.

Reber and his co-founders sold Wunderlist’s parent company, 6Wunderkinder, to Microsoft in 2015 for a reported $100 million to $200 million. In 2019, as Microsoft prepared to shut the app down, he publicly asked Satya Nadella to sell it back. Microsoft kept it, then retired it in favor of To Do.

Now some of those former Wunderlist owners may end up back with the people who built it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, within hours of Huang’s original (and ignominious) exit from Nvidia earlier this month, a “Stand With Jensen” petition circulated online, demanding Huang’s return to the company he’d cofounded in 1993.
  • Travis Kalanick, Uber’s pugnacious cofounder and former CEO, was both a signatory and especially vocal in his support.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy led to his ouster from Nvidia. Eleven days later, he’s back—the outcome Silicon Valley founders, watchers, and luminaries wanted all along.

In a recent development, within hours of Huang’s original (and ignominious) exit from Nvidia earlier this month, a “Stand With Jensen” petition circulated online, demanding Huang’s return to the company he’d cofounded in 1993. Signatories included Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke, Atreides Management CIO Gavin Baker, and Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi, who wrote in the comments, “Nvidia runs on Jensen! Bring him back!”.

Travis Kalanick, Uber’s pugnacious cofounder and former CEO, was both a signatory and especially vocal in his support.

According to recent reports, “Jensen is one of the great builders of our time,” Kalanick—himself ousted in 2017 from Uber amid compounding scandals—wrote in a public post on the “Stand With Jensen” site. “Liberty and civilizational progress depend on Jensen,” Kalanick declared. “He has erred, yes—to err is to be human—but I do not believe anything he has done rises to the bar of separating him from his company. Jensen deserves fairness in adjudication and we must presume innocence until that adjudication proves otherwise beyond a reasonable doubt.”.

According to recent reports, huang’s return is a Rorschach test of sorts. Some critics see a corporate governance nightmare, while much of the wider public has memed or expressed horror at the circumstances of Huang’s initial resignation (widely described as potentially raising national security concerns). In Silicon Valley though, Huang’s ouster was an injustice that trumped any other aspects of the story. To tech, Huang remains the most indispensable of founders, a nearly godlike figure in a culture that worships “founder mode.”.

According to recent reports, so, Huang’s return, however questionable it may be, is cause for celebration. Even the very circumspect Sam Altman, who’d previously expressed cautious sympathy for Huang (and who of course, went through a very similar ordeal), tweeted on X on Monday, “Jensen!” Musk, meanwhile, tweeted: “The mistake has been corrected.” Sarah Guo, the plugged-in founder of Conviction VC, welcomed Huang back. The chorus from tech was, in its way, relatively unanimous about just how positive this news was. (The markets agreed vigorously; Nvidia closed today up about 31%, after last week’s massive tech rout.) Meanwhile, for Nvidia’s board, it’s a dicey U-turn.

In a recent development, “Six days after Nvidia’s board stated it had no intention of reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, he’s back—before the board’s own independent investigation has reported anything, before he answers questions from Congress next week, and with no conditions attached (or at least none that anyone outside the boardroom can see),” said Nicole Bestard, founder of communications firm Quarter Horse Strategies, via email. “From a reputation standpoint, this is a huge mistake. It asks investors, employees, and the public to take the board’s judgment on faith.”.

The move from here, in part, is likely to attempt to bury this, David Tepper, cofounder and CEO of Ascerta, predicts.

Sources indicate that “It very likely means that Nvidia will be putting out their next GPU cycle (the 6000 series) much sooner than otherwise expected,” he mentioned via email. “They will be eager to bury the news cycle with Nvidia’s continued dominance in the space versus keeping the attention on his infidelity.”.

Nevertheless, things are not likely to be the same from here on out, noted Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures.

“No one can replace the vision he has,” noted Padval. “With him back, he may not go back to 100% immediately, he’ll likely be more cautious. It will still be significantly better than a few weeks back.”.

Translation: We still can’t assume Huang will continue to be as aggressive an investor, operator, and guarantor as he may have been before, even with a supposed return to normalcy.

According to recent reports, “The private markets ecosystem has to stand by itself,” said Padval. “This was driven by Nvidia a lot in the past, the whole AI ecosystem. If participation is less, the venture community needs to step it up with conviction. We all need to believe in the companies we’re backing. And if we believe in the companies, [we] don’t have to wait for the signal from Nvidia.”.

Industry News: AI Is Accelerating Software Development — But Businesses Need a Better Way to Measure the Quality of What They Ship

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (860 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Entrepreneur

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.
  • For the last decade, the way engineering performance has been reported to leadership has followed a stable pattern.
  • By 2027, the boards of software companies will be asking a different question.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

For the last decade, the way engineering performance has been reported to leadership has followed a stable pattern. Some version of the four DORA metrics — deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore — has anchored the conversation. Engineering leaders track them. Finance leaders learn to read them. Boards nod at them.

That pattern is about to break.

By 2027, the boards of software companies will be asking a different question. The question will not be “how fast are we deploying?” It will be “how much of what we deploy is actually verified?” And the reason for the shift is not fashion. It is that AI-assisted development has made the current metrics quietly unreliable, and the market is waking up to it.

Two major datasets show how far the dashboard has drifted from reality:.

On a typical board dashboard, the throughput gains appear as headline numbers while the instability sits in a footnote. A director reading deployment frequency would see an organization getting faster, with no view of the review process thinning out underneath it.

DORA has acknowledged the gap. Its researchers introduced deployment rework rate, the proportion of deployments that are unplanned fixes, as a fifth measure in 2024. DORA’s Nathen Harvey said on DX’s Engineering Enablement podcast that the four keys aren’t sufficient on their own for understanding AI’s impact.

Rework rate is worth tracking, but it records the fix only after a customer has already hit the bug. It can’t warn you before a release.

In a recent development, code coverage reports how much of a codebase some test executed. It states nothing about whether that test checked an outcome a customer cares about, and AI-generated test suites can push coverage up without improving that second question.

A suite can touch every branch of a checkout service and still never confirm that a customer paying in a second currency gets charged the right amount.

You build verification coverage from the customer side. Product, engineering and finance agree on the journeys that make or lose money: signup, checkout, the core action the product exists for and the permission flows enterprise buyers probe during procurement.

Each journey gets an expected outcome written in business terms, such as an order confirmed at the correct price or an invited user landing with the right role. For each release, the team records how many of those journeys it ran end to end on the release candidate, in real browsers and devices, and how many produced that outcome.

A CFO can read the result without a glossary: something like “47 of 52 revenue-critical journeys verified before release.” Because your team measures it before anything ships, it should move ahead of rework rate and change failure rate, which register problems only after customers find them.

Part of the pressure comes from outside engineering. Cyber underwriters have started asking CFOs how they are managing AI risk.

It has been revealed that directors who signed off on AI tooling budgets will also start asking what the spend bought besides volume. A rising deployment count tells them the team ships more often. Verification coverage tells them whether the product customers pay for still works.

Most teams can produce a first figure within a quarter by following four steps:.

Agentic test automation platforms such as KaneAI now let teams run these journeys against the rendered product on every release candidate.

It has been revealed that DORA metrics still belong on the dashboard, because they tell you how fast and how steadily your organization delivers. Add verification coverage beside them in your next monthly report, and protect it from the pressure every board metric attracts.

Industry observers note that A team under pressure can raise its score by shortening the journey list. Require product and finance sign-off before anyone changes it, and show the list size next to the ratio.

Include the failure cases customers hit, such as a declined card or an expired session, because a journey verified only on its happy path tells the board less than the number suggests.

Expect the score to sit below 100%, and tell directors which journeys failed and why. When they ask what AI has changed, you can show them how much of what shipped was verified to work.

That pattern is about to break.

Microsoft’s final Outlook outage report details testing gaps and safeguards that backfired

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1015 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 21, 2026 at 9:31 amNovember 21, 2026 at 9:50 am.
  • The bug behind last week’s global Microsoft 365 outage struck only newer, more powerful servers in a key part of Microsoft’s network.
  • One reason Microsoft didn’t catch it in advance: it was testing on older servers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 21, 2026 at 9:31 amNovember 21, 2026 at 9:50 am.

The bug behind last week’s global Microsoft 365 outage struck only newer, more powerful servers in a key part of Microsoft’s network. That’s because it created a kind of traffic jam inside each server, and the more work a machine tried to do at once, the worse the jam got. The newer servers are built to do more at once, so they’re the ones that seized up.

One reason Microsoft didn’t catch it in advance: it was testing on older servers.

“Our testing did not adequately represent the combination of hardware and traffic mix encountered during this incident,” the organization acknowledged in its final report, released Friday evening, a week after resolving the outage that crippled Outlook and cut off email for people around the world.

Recent findings suggest that testing that more closely replicates the company’s production environment is one of 13 next steps in the report — measures the company claims it will take to keep it from happening again. The list is also aimed at reassuring the businesses that rely on Microsoft for email and collaboration, after CEO Satya Nadella acknowledged at the company’s Ignite conference this week that it has work to do on resilience.

Many of the other steps identified in the report go after a bigger problem: during the incident, the safeguards meant to contain the failure spread it around the world instead.

In a recent development, what set it off: As detailed in Microsoft’s preliminary report last weekend, the bug at the center of the outage had been sitting dormant since July, when Microsoft started rolling out the software update that introduced it. For more than three months, it caused no problems.

The bug affected the servers that make up what Microsoft calls its network gateway, a front door that connects people to Outlook email and other Microsoft 365 services. The flaw came from a Windows patch used only on those servers. Standard versions of Windows weren’t affected.

Industry observers note that so what was the bug? Microsoft’s final report gives a partial answer, saying it came from a change to how the gateway servers handle incoming connections.

Under heavy load, it turned out, the Windows process that sets up those connections bogged down, with tasks stuck waiting on each other until the servers ran out of computing power and memory and stopped responding.

The final report doesn’t say what the July upgrade was meant to fix. But it does lay out three conditions that finally set the bug off. Without the bug, even all three together would have been routine, the report states.

Recent findings suggest that first, nearly 14% of the gateway’s server capacity was already offline that day for routine software updates. That’s normally not a problem, because Microsoft keeps enough spare capacity to absorb it. But it meant fewer servers were available to carry the load.

That’s a different explanation from the preliminary report, which blamed the missing capacity on an unrelated problem.

Second, all of Microsoft Teams’ traffic landed on those same servers. Teams normally runs through a separate gateway of its own. About 15 hours before the outage, a routing glitch on that Teams gateway in Microsoft’s US East region set off an automatic switch that moved all Teams traffic worldwide onto the servers that handle email.

Third, the U.S. workday got going. Widespread failures began around 8 a.m. Pacific, as traffic in North America climbed toward its daily peak.

Recent findings suggest that how it spread: As servers stopped responding, Microsoft’s systems automatically moved their traffic to healthy servers nearby, which had the same bug and buckled under the extra load. At the low point, more than 80% of the gateway’s servers in North America were unresponsive.

The system then shifted traffic to other regions, spreading the problem further.

“Within about two hours of the broad failures that began in North America, servers in every region were affected globally,” the report says.

It has been revealed that the preliminary report had blamed that spread partly on “a separate glitch.” The final report doesn’t repeat or explain that phrase. Instead, its findings say the way Microsoft distributes traffic “can cascade failures to other regions.”.

Once the servers went down, getting them back up was its own problem. As servers came back online, they were swamped by pent-up demand and froze again, a pattern engineers call a “thundering herd.” Microsoft indicates it will ease traffic back onto recovering servers gradually. That fix doesn’t have a date yet.

The fixes: To keep a failure from spreading again, Microsoft indicates it will change how its systems shift traffic between regions, so a problem in one part of the world stays there.

Industry observers note that it also aims to split up the servers that handle email, so a surge from another service like Teams can’t take them down. And Teams will switch over only in the region that has the problem, not worldwide.

Some of the fixes are due by the end of the year, others by the end of March. Several don’t have a date yet.

Sources indicate that microsoft indicates its first notice to customers went out about 20 minutes after the outage took hold, and it looks to shorten that by the end of the year. No business email was lost, according to the report, though some delayed messages to consumer mailboxes that had been inactive for more than 30 days bounced back to senders.

The report also confirms what Microsoft said the day after the outage began: it wasn’t hackers, and it wasn’t AI. “This incident was confirmed not to be caused by a cyberattack, and we found no evidence of malicious activity,” it says. “This change was not caused by AI tooling.”.

The upcoming testing is supposed to be in place by the end of March, according to the final report. This time, the company says, the machines in the lab will actually match the ones running the service in production.

The 11 days that brought Jensen Huang back to Nvidia

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Last Wednesday, Elon Musk, appearing as flustered as ever, called Nvidia’s decision to push out founder Jensen Huang a huge mistake, comparing it to the Chicago Bulls dumping Michael Jordan during a winning streak.
  • “There’s no one that can really replace Jensen.
  • Five days later, Musk was posting on X, the social media platform he owns, to celebrate Huang’s return.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last Wednesday, Elon Musk, appearing as flustered as ever, called Nvidia’s decision to push out founder Jensen Huang a huge mistake, comparing it to the Chicago Bulls dumping Michael Jordan during a winning streak.

“There’s no one that can really replace Jensen. He does the roles of several people,” Musk told the New York Times‘ Andrew Ross Sorkin, appearing at the newspaper’s DealBook summit via videoconference while Musk was in China with President Trump. “He has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades. He understands the technology incredibly well.”.

Five days later, Musk was posting on X, the social media platform he owns, to celebrate Huang’s return.

According to recent reports, “It is done,” he wrote. “The mistake has been corrected.”.

According to recent reports, musk’s reaction reflects the extraordinary political muscle that he and other powerful figures in Silicon Valley and Washington flexed to bring Huang back. The Nvidia board reinstated Huang as CEO, the manufacturer revealed Monday. His ouster, initially triggered by an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, has gripped the business and political worlds for the past two weeks, and his return promises more shockwaves in the tech industry and the halls of power. Since Huang’s resignation was announced on Nov. 12, influential figures, from Musk to Trump, have waged a pressure campaign to make Huang CEO again, even as Nvidia’s board said it had moved on. Trump even called the board as it deliberated Huang’s reinstatement to push for his return.

The reversal caps one of the most remarkable resurgences in business history, while raising numerous questions about how the firm moves forward, given an internal investigation into Huang and a reported probe into Nvidia’s accounting by the Securities and Exchange Commission.

This is a reconstruction of Huang’s ouster and return as it unfolded over a momentous 11-day period:.

On Oct. 29, the New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence officials had concluded that Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, was passing information to the Chinese government, and that she had a close relationship with Jensen Huang. The Times also reported that Trump was briefed roughly a year earlier but didn’t act. Subsequent reporting detailed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited Alice Huang to gather intelligence on Nvidia’s CEO and possibly lobby for the sale of advanced chips to China.

After the Times report, Huang told Bloomberg News there was nothing unusual about his relationship with Alice Huang, likening it to his dealings with Chinese customers and executives.

“It was all completely normal and not unusual,” he said.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 8, Huang publicly admitted to an affair, writing that “there is no excuse for what I did” and pledging to cooperate fully with Nvidia’s investigation, which the board revealed the same day. The board, overseen by independent directors with outside counsel, mentioned it had “no reason to believe” national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. The next day, Chinese officials dismissed the spying claims as “pure fabrication out of thin air.”.

On Nov. 10, the independent directors hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to run the investigation. The tech news website The Information reported that Alice Huang’s network had built companies to buy Nvidia chips, helping arrange about $7.5 billion in purchases, including of banned chips.

The next day, the Times reported, citing five people who worked at Nvidia, that Huang had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who has reported directly to him. Reached by phone, Huang told the Times, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly” and hung up. Later that day, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s 10-member board was preparing to push Huang out and had called an emergency meeting. The alleged affair with Powell violated the manufacturer’s code of conduct, and Huang’s earlier assurances appeared to be false.

According to recent reports, by the next morning, Nvidia confirmed Huang had resigned. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress became interim CEO, and tech entrepreneur Harvey Jones was named Nvidia’s first board chair. The same day, Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) and Rep. Richard E. Neal (D-Mass.) announced an inquiry into the administration’s approval of Nvidia’s H200 chip sales to China. Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.) asked Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify.

It has been revealed that hours after the resignation, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second, unnamed Nvidia employee. It also reported that Huang misled Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter and Chief Marketing Officer Alison Wagonfeld in both fall 2025 and October 2026.

Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14.35% in intraday trading, wiping out about $600 billion in value at the low, and ultimately closed down 4.34%.

Recent findings suggest that almost as soon as Huang was ousted, a comeback effort took shape among tech and political elites and Nvidia’s own staff. A week ago, President Trump told reporters he would support reinstating Huang. “I would certainly not mind seeing that,” Trump said, adding that Huang had “learned a massive lesson.”.

Industry observers note that an Nvidia employee rolled out a website with an open letter demanding that the board reinstate Huang. As of Monday, more than 206,000 names appeared on the letter. Signatories included Musk, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, Shopify CEO Tobias Lutke, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and tech investor Gavin Baker.

The day after Huang resigned, Baker and Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner remarked in an open letter that Huang “has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known.”.

The same day, Nvidia’s board released a statement saying it was hiring an executive search firm and hadn’t yet approached any potential candidates.

Last Tuesday, Huang broke his silence, posting on X that he was sorry for “serious mistakes” in his personal life and pledging to cooperate with the board’s investigation.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote.

The same day, Nvidia reported blockbuster earnings, with revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103%. Interim CEO Kress remarked the “roadmap is on track” and that Nvidia had stopped shipping AI chips to China. Jones, the board chair, said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and that Heidrick & Struggles was running the search for the next chief executive. Nvidia also created a board committee on national security and export controls, chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson.

Industry observers note that later that day, the Journal reported that the SEC is investigating Nvidia, including whether its disclosures misled investors. On Thursday, California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia, seeking answers on whether China received chips or confidential information and whether investors were misled. The next day, the Times reported that Huang routinely humiliated employees, with violent threats and settlements. His spokesperson denied one fired employee’s allegations.

According to recent reports, last week, the S&P 500 tumbled 8.6%, its worst week since April 2025. The Nasdaq sank about 10% and the Dow 8%, the Nasdaq’s worst week since March 2020. The selloff reflected broader concerns about the AI industry, which came amid Anthropic’s initial public offering on Thursday and post-midterm-election selling, as well as investors treating Huang as a stand-in for the AI trade.

Throughout the week, tech leaders kept praising Huang and urging his return.

At a Tuesday roundtable in San Francisco that included Fortune, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella hailed Huang as “a singular person” who has contributed immensely to the tech industry, and noted it was up to Nvidia’s board to decide what happened next. On Wednesday, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey called for Huang to return during the Times‘ DealBook summit, saying that getting rid of Huang only benefited China.

On Sunday, Trump posted on Truth Social calling for Huang to be rehired. On Monday, Trump told CNBC he had been talking with the board and Huang, and that the board had been reasonable.

“I believe my intervention was very important,” Trump remarked, adding that the U.S. national security team doesn’t believe Huang is a national security threat. Trump said he worked with Vice President JD Vance and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to get Huang back. According to Semafor, Trump actually dialed in to the board meeting on Sunday in which the decision was made to bring Huang back. White House communications director Steven Cheung told Fortune that Trump was “totally involved.”.

Although Huang is back as CEO, the Commerce Department Monday added Megaspeed to a blacklist that will bar it from receiving Nvidia chips without having a government license.

According to recent reports, huang appeared at Nvidia’s Santa Clara, Calif. headquarters on Monday soon after his reinstatement was announced.

Sources indicate that “Thank you all for a second chance,” he said to a room full of employees, many cheering. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”.

Sources indicate that by the close of markets, the S&P 500 had gained 4.7% and the Nasdaq 6.5%, the best day for both since April 2025. The recovery gained back roughly half of the S&P’s losses from last week and more than half of the Nasdaq’s. Nvidia shares rose more than 30%, to close at $165.05.

On Truth Social, Trump posted an altered image that put Huang’s face on the famous photo of Trump raising his fist after the 2024 assassination attempt. In the doctored image, Huang is holding a red bra.

Shiba Inu's on-chain holders increased as the number of wallets holding SHIB hit 1,700,930 on November 19, 2026.

According to the latest figures shared by Etherscan SHIB, an X account dedicated to providing updates on the SHIB ecosystem, the cryptocurrency added 236 upcoming on-chain holders in a single day, taking its total past the 1.7 million milestone.

Recent findings suggest that the month of November has also seen consistent growth, with SHIB adding 4,520 holders since the start of the month. The broader 2026 trend is even more pronounced, with the number of holders of the token increasing by 152,300 since the beginning of the year.

While Shiba Inu's latest milestone seems remarkable, Mazrael suggested that the Shib ecosystem, including Shibarium, might have more holders than indicated, with 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on the BNB Chain.

In a recent development, "Shibarium has more holders than those you listed, though. But yeah. Well, there are also 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on BNB. But that's not actually CCIP SHIB; it is a peg," Mazrael wrote.

Tech Report: 5 Powerful Lessons Leaders Can Learn From People Who Pay It Forward

💡 Key Takeaways
